#2062. ‘I want to…’ – Virgil van Dijk issues Liverpool contract hint as mega decision awaits

Virgil van Dijk has spoken about his long-term future at Liverpool, where he now has less than eight months remaining on his current contract.

Having penned a two-year extension in April 2025, the club captain is once again approaching a major crossroads in his illustrious career as the clock ticks towards the juncture at which a decision will have to be made.

Fellow stalwart Alisson Becker has voiced his desire to remain with the Reds beyond next summer, with his agent in ‘preliminary talks‘ over a potential new deal for the goalkeeper, although the Dutch defender has been rather more coy about his own situation.

Van Dijk addressed his long-term future when speaking to reporters after Liverpool’s 3-1 victory at Crystal Palace.

In quotes published by the Liverpool Echo on Tuesday, the 35-year-old said: “I feel good but it’s not about me at the moment. Let’s see. I’m not in any panic whatsoever. I want to keep playing and continue what I’m doing.

“Let’s see what the season brings. I’ve had an amazing time already so far. If that will be extended, that’s the case. If not, then I will go somewhere else. There’s nothing to report at the moment but that doesn’t mean that there’s any stress or anything.”

(Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Publicly at least, Van Dijk is giving nothing away about his future, with the Liverpool captain seemingly happy to stay on but also keeping his options open in case a new deal with the Reds can’t be agreed upon.

It’d certainly represent a break from the norm from Anfield chiefs to offer a lucrative contract extension to a player who’s already on £350,000 per week (Capology) and who’ll turn 36 next summer, but we’re not talking about any ordinary footballer here.

The captain is one of the greatest to ever pull on the iconic red shirt, and aside from an uncharacteristic error against Villarreal last month, he’s been imperious alongside Jeremy Jacquet at the heart of our defence this season.

The Frenchman is among several young centre-backs in line to ultimately succeed Van Dijk as our defensive general in the years to come (along with Giovanni Leoni and Ifeanyi Ndukwe), but the influence of the experienced Dutchman is still clear.

If the skipper’s preference would be to continue with Liverpool into next season, then hopefully he and the club can reach an agreement which’d keep him at Anfield beyond the end of this campaign.

#2057. Bayern won’t sign Rio Ngumoha after missing their chance in the summer – opinion

Bayern Munich are reportedly confident that there is a deal to be done with Liverpool for talented youngster Rio Ngumoha.

The Reds were understood to be the subject of some probing from the Bavarian giants, with discussions said to have taken place with the winger’s brother.

Whether Liverpool feel the same way… well, let’s just be clear on this: they don’t.

As Mick Brown noted in his latest report with Football Insider: “From what I hear, Bayern Munich are pretty confident there is a deal to be done.

“When there’s all this talk about making contact with his agents, speaking to the player, what it might cost, that stuff doesn’t happen unless they think they can do a deal.

“Whether Liverpool feel the same way, I have my doubts, because he has such obvious potential and Andoni Iraola has been pretty clear he is part of his plans.

“I don’t think he’s the finished article, but not many players are at 18, there are still areas of his game where he has to improve, so maybe that’s where the speculation comes from.”

Mick goes on to note that the Reds are currently giving Ngumoha everything he could realistically hope for at an elite European outfit. There is a pathway to the senior team and he’s already picked up 642 minutes (Transfermarkt) of action in the famous red shirt this season.

On top of that, his all-round game is being carefully developed, with appearances roughly split between both flanks.

And most importantly? Liverpool aren’t burning the player out — Andoni Iraola is managing the teenager’s minutes, rotating alongside Bradley Barcola, Victor Munoz and Cody Gakpo.

So, Bayern may feel a deal can be done, but realistically, can they offer the 18-year-old substantially more than he’s already receiving at Liverpool?

It’s worth pointing out that, as is indeed the case across Europe’s biggest outfits, Bayern’s shortlist is far from limited to Liverpool’s No.73. Names like Antonio Nusa and Oskar Pietuszewski are also highly rated by the club, with the former thought to be well-admired by Bayern chief Max Eberl.

But the important distinction to make here is that Ngumoha will not come cheap – far from it, compared to the two names alone we’ve just listed. And if Bayern already valued the versatile winger at €70m [£58.3m] in the summer, can you imagine how much his value has skyrocketed since becoming an important part of Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool squad? We’re surely talking in the territory of at least upwards of £7om, at a conservative estimate.

On that basis, options like Pietuszewski – who reportedly has a €60m [£50.1m] release clause at FC Porto – surely start to look more feasible for a club like Bayern that doesn’t necessarily have the same level of cash to splash as its Premier League counterparts.

Newcastle United star Anthony Elanga has given an update on his comeback from injury.

The winger picked up an injury back in September during a Newcastle United training session and has now revealed to media in Sweden: “It was an injury that was a little difficult to identify, it was in the groin, but I came back faster than anyone thought.”

It was just ahead of kick-off on 14 September 2026 away against Leeds at Elland Road that we found out Anthony Elanga had picked up a mystery injury.

Elanga having helped United to an excellent start to the season with three wins and two draws in the opening five games, with the Sweden star scoring in the Premier League matches against both Liverpool and Tottenham.

A ridiculous number of injuries for Matthias Jaissle to cope with so early in the season, as days after that defeat at Leeds, the Newcastle United boss had nine players ruled out for the Hull match which United won 2-1.

There was talk of Anthony Elanga potentially missing a large part of the season but instead he only two more matches after that Hull one.

A day less than six weeks after missing the Leeds match, Elanga playing the final 13 minutes of the win at Palace, then the second half at Everton in the Carabao Cup, first 76 minutes at home to Everton in the Premier League, last five minutes at Fulham.

Anthony Elanga telling Fotbollskanalen: “I took care of myself very well. I ate well, I rest well. The medical team at my club team was very good with me and the cooperation with my own team that I work with off the pitch [was good]. It was a strange injury and I’m just happy to be back.”

Anthony Elanga asked if he is still feeling the injury today: “Nothing. I now feel healthy, 120 per cent. I’m back now and…it is about getting into the same momentum that I had at the start of the season. Now I’m happy to be here, back with the national team, and building on that momentum.”

Anthony Elanga missed the Nations League matches in the last international window with Sweden but is now part of the squad that will face Bosnia-Herzegovina and Poland.

#2052. “I’m told…” – Transfer insider says Liverpool stalwart has ‘every chance’ of getting new deal

One transfer insider has talked up the probability of Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk signing a new contract at Anfield in the next few months.

The 35-year-old’s current deal with the Reds expires at the end of this season, and he seemed relaxed over his future when discussing the topic with reporters after the win over Crystal Palace on Sunday.

That update from the skipper comes just as Alisson Becker (whose contract is also due to expire in 2027) voiced his desire to remain on Merseyside beyond then, with the goalkeeper’s agent opening talks over a prospective extension.

Speaking on The TEAMtalk podcast, Graeme Bailey claimed that Van Dijk has a strong chance of securing a new contract at Liverpool due to the positive impact that his performances have had on young centre-back partner Jeremy Jacquet.

The reporter said of the Dutchman: “Obviously he’s out of contract in the summer. He’s gonna be another year older as well. He signed a huge contract back in 2025.

“Everyone thought this might be his final farewell tour, but he’s actually had a very good season. It’s part of the reason why we’re seeing Jeremy Jacquet playing ever so well. You’ve got [Giovanni] Leoni there as well, the young Italian central defender.

“From what I’m hearing, Andoni Iraola really wants to keep [Van Dijk] around. Captain figure – it’s like having a coach on the pitch. He’s not missing any games; he’s playing really well.

“I’m told there’s every chance he gets another 12 months at least. It doesn’t stop them [from] bringing another centre-half in, but learning from Van Dijk, these youngsters… I’m told Jacquet is learning so much playing next to him.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

That Bailey spoke of how Jacquet is learning plentifully from Van Dijk speaks volumes for the continued importance of the captain to this Liverpool side.

A number of experienced stalwarts have left over the past couple of years, most notably Mo Salah and Andy Robertson at the end of last season, so the ongoing presence of the Dutchman brings a much-needed sense of stability to a team which has undergone significant transition since the start of 2025.

If the 35-year-old agrees a new deal at Anfield, it won’t be a case of sentimentality clouding the club’s judgement – FSG are notoriously reluctant to hand out lucrative contract extensions to players over 30, so for the skipper to even have a plausible chance of getting one says a lot for the influence that he still exerts on the pitch.

Van Dijk is more than experienced enough to not give anything away publicly unless he’s sure that there are major developments behind the scenes about his future, so it doesn’t surprise us that he’s been coy on the subject.

A decision will need to be reached before the season ends, but considering that he didn’t pen his previous extension until two months from his prior deal expiring, there’s still ample time for the defender to agree new terms with Liverpool and continue his hallowed legacy into the 2027/28 campaign at least.

#2047. Liverpool injury update: Virgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch, Dominik Szoboszlai latest news and return dates

Liverpool will be battling some significant fitness issues during the international break.

The two-week pause in the campaign may have not come at an ideal time for Liverpool after bouncing back from successive defeats to Arsenal and Fenerbahce by beating Crystal Palace 3-1 at the weekend.

Nevertheless, it’s a chance for Andoni Iraola to take stock of where his team is at and build towards a huge game at home to a Manchester United side currently in the Premier League relegation zone.

The Spaniard has made it clear that his one wish from the final international break of the year is no fresh injuries - particularly after losing Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai during the autumn window.

However, Iraola may not get his wish upon news that captain Virgil van Dijk has withdrawn from the Netherlands squad, while Szoboszlai is awaiting results of an assessment after joining up with the Hungary squad.

With that in mind, here is the latest Liverpool injury news and return dates…

The Liverpool captain was called up by new Dutch head coach Xavi for the Nations League double-header against Greece and Germany.

However, it was confirmed on Monday that he - and Sunderland striker Brian Brobbey - had pulled out of the squad for fitness related reasons.

A statement reads: “Virgil van Dijk and Brian Brobbey have been dropped from the Dutch national team's upcoming international matches. Both players did not return fit from the past weekend's matches and are therefore unavailable.

“The squad thus currently consists of 23 players.”

Liverpool fans will be hopeful this decision is no more than a precaution, particularly after Van Dijk played 90 minutes in all four Nations League games during the autumn international window.

Potential return date: Sunday November 22, vs Manchester United (H)

Szoboszlai will be assessed to determine his fitness for international duty with Hungary.

The midfielder was forced off in the second half against Palace due to a knee complaint and Iraola admitted afterwards that the Reds No8 was not fully fit.

“Dom definitely wasn’t 100 per cent in the second half,” Iraola said. "Let’s see. The last thing we need now is to lose players in the international games.

"In the last international break we lost three very important players in Alex (Isak), Cody (Gakpo) and Dom. So now I'm praying - it's the last thing we need.”

Potential return date: Sunday November 22, vs Manchester United (H)

Ryan Gravenberch has missed Liverpool’s last two games with a heel injury. There was hope the Dutchman would return for the trip to Selhurst Park, but was ultimately left out of the matchday squad.

“The only doubt we will have is Ryan,” Iraola said in the pre-Crystal Palace press conference. “The others will be the same as we have been.

“The Ryan Gravenberch thing is a day-to-day thing, it’s a matter of pain. Let’s see if he can deal with the pain and he can help us.”

With the injury severe enough to prevent the midfielder from being called up by Xavi for the Netherlands’ Nations League double-header, Gravenberch must be considered a major doubt to face Man United.

Potential return date: Sunday November 22, vs Manchester United (H)

Jeremie Frimpong picked up a muscle injury during the comeback win over Brentford last month, resulting in another lay-off for the full-back since his arrival from Bayer Leverkusen.

Like compatriots Van Dijk and Gravenberch, he will not be representing the Dutch during the international break and it’s believed his return is not too far away.

In the most recent update of Frimpong, Iraola said: “Jeremie Frimpong is obviously a new muscle injury and it happened, I think, in the second or third minute he was playing, difficult to predict and we will have to wait until he recovers.

“But it’s going to be difficult, I think, before the [November international] break. We will try but it’s going to be difficult to have him.”

Potential return date: Sunday November 22, vs Manchester United (H)

Giovanno Leoni signed for Liverpool from Parma last summer in a deal worth around £26million, but a serious knee injury means he has been limited to just one senior appearance so far.

The centre-back made his debut in the Carabao Cup against Southampton in September 2025, but he was stretchered off and it was later confirmed that he had suffered an anterior cruciate ligament tear.

He was expected to miss a full year of action, which has proved to be the case.

He had hoped to have made his comeback for the recent September international break, but that has since been delayed.

“It’s taking more time than we wanted,” Iraola said. “The planning was to train with the team in this past international break [but] probably it’s going to be in the next international break, so we’ve lost one month in the process.

“Giovanni’s injury, I wasn’t here but talking to the medical department, it was not just an ACL – it was a bad injury, a lot of things around the knee were involved apart from the ACL.”

Hugo Ekitike has not played since rupturing his Achilles against Paris Saint-Germain in April.

The Frenchman was forced to sit out the end of last season and the World Cup, where it was estimated that he would be out for nine months to a full year.

He was included in Iraola’s squad for the Champions League league phase - which came as a surprise to many - with the hope that he could potentially return for the final two games in January, against Inter Milan and Lens.

The striker is thought to be targeting a comeback before the turn of the year.

Conor Bradley is another long-term absentee for Liverpool, having suffered a serious knee injury at Arsenal back in January.

The Northern Ireland international suffered bone and ligament damage in that match, which has kept him out for almost a year.

Iraola’s latest comments were positive, indicating that Bradley will soon return to full training.

“[He is] doing very well,” Iraola said. “I think [he is] in a good place. Conor is not so far from training with the group – not like full training but doing some things with the group.

“I think Conor is not very far from starting doing things with us."

It looks as though he could rejoin team training during the November international break.

Potential return date: Wednesday, December 2 vs Sunderland (H)

#2043. Andy Robertson was left with a ‘headache’ after two Liverpool games last season that he ‘hated’

Andy Robertson has said that there were two Liverpool matches in particular last season that he ‘hated’, having been left with a ‘headache’ after both.

The Reds were beaten twice by Galatasaray in the 2025/26 Champions League, with a pair of 1-0 defeats at RAMS Park in the league phase in September and the round of 16 first leg in March (Arne Slot’s team won the return fixture 4-0 a week later).

Both matches were almost clones of one another, with the Merseysiders conceding an early goal and being unable to restore parity after putting in a subdued performance.

Now of Tottenham Hotspur, Robertson reflected on the two visits to Istanbul last season and how he was left with a migraine from the incessant intimidation from the natives.

The Scottish left-back said (via Fanatik): “I hated playing against Galatasaray last season. The Galatasaray away game was terrible. They booed non-stop throughout the entire match. Believe me, you leave the match with a headache.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The city of Istanbul has left an indelible mark in Liverpool’s European history from the epic 2005 Champions League final against AC Milan, but recent visits to the Turkish capital have been bruising.

The Reds twice relinquished a lead to lose 3-2 away to Fenerbahce last week, and the two trips to play Galatasaray last season were galling, to say the least.

Pat Nevin justifiably claimed that the 1-0 league phase defeat ‘could have been worse‘ given the nature of our defending that night, and John Aldridge described the repeat of that scoreline in the knockout phase eight months ago as a ‘horrible watch‘.

Slot had warned about the febrile atmosphere of RAMS Park prior to the latter fixture, remarking: “Sometimes you wonder if this could be done by human people”, and for a player of Robertson’s character and experience to be so rattled by the intensity of the home support is quite telling.

With Galatasaray currently 18th in the league phase standings, it’s not inconceivable that they and Liverpool could meet at some point in the knockout rounds yet again next spring, but we’d imagine that the Reds have had their fill of visits to Istanbul after the past 14 months.

Kasper Hogh must respond at Celtic as concerns continue to emerge over his ability to perform in Scotland.

That is the opinion of former Tottenham, Everton and Aston Villa scout and Scandinavian football expert, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

The 25-year-old joined the Hoops from Bodo/Glimt for a fee in the region of £11million in the summer transfer window, and got off to the perfect start when he scored a hat-trick against Kilmarnock in his second game.

#2038. Two Chelsea summer deals to 'blame' for attacking struggles - recruitment expert

The sales of Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson are beginning to look like strange pieces of business for Chelsea.

That is the opinion of experienced former Tottenham, Aston Villa and Everton scout, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

The Blues were happy to part ways with both strikers but have been left short in attack, winning just one game from their last four without Joao Pedro.

Jackson was sold to Villa in a deal worth up to £65million and the 25-year-old has scored nine goals in his first 14 games for his new club, including four in his last three Premier League games.

Few would have argued with the sales of Delap and Jackson in the summer, with both players outcast at Stamford Bridge.

But it was expected that at least one of them would be replaced, with Xabi Alonso now resigned to opt for makeshift solutions in the absence of Pedro.

The Spaniard does have the option of Danny Welbeck, but has been hesitant to give the striker more than a brief appearance off the bench.

"They sold Delap, then they sold Jackson and they've only got one out and out centre-forward, really," King told Football Insider.

Whether that will require the Spaniard to swallow his pride and trust Welbeck, it remains to be seen.

#2032. Liverpool fans have Alexander Isak concerns for all the wrong reasons as data shows

Correspondent AUTHORITY Sports journalist with experience at GamingINTEL and GRV Media; University of Wolverhampton graduate. FOCUS Data content, opinion, and general news coverage across the Breaking Media network. THE INSIGHT Scott utilises a network of club and industry contacts to deliver verified, broad-spectrum reporting. He provides the data and opinion foundations behind the headlines to ensure fans get the full story as it happens.

Alexander Isak is doing the job he was brought to Liverpool to do, and that is scoring goals.

However, there are plenty of people out there who are becoming concerned with his lack of involvement throughout games.

Supporters spent many years seeing the work of Roberto Firmino leading the attack, while even the likes of Darwin Nunez were often hailed for his work rate too.

A striker pressing from the front has been synonymous with the Anfield side.

But, truthfully, that is not Isak's style, and it is no longer how Liverpool wants to play.

And it is working wonders for Andoni Iraola's side this season, with fans needing to take a step back from their concerns.

Liverpool are having a strong season under Iraola, but questions over Isak continue to be brought up.

Supporters growing frustrated with Isak's lack of involvement in games are completely missing the point.

This is no longer Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool, but rather how Iraola wants his team to play.

As per FotMob, Isak is on the lower end of touches per 90, coming in at the 11.4th percentile with 25.2.

But he is the second-top goalscorer in the Premier League with seven goals.

His job is to occupy positions and defenders, and ultimately make the most of the few touches he gets.

Not every striker needs to be heavily involved in build-up play, and there are different ways for Liverpool to play in a way that unites the fans.

Just because he is not touching the ball often does not mean he is not involved.

Ultimately, for Isak as well, Liverpool are not putting as much focus into their attacks down the middle of the pitch.

As WhoScored shares, the Reds frequently go down the left side much more often, with 39 per cent of their attacks on that wing.

The right-wing sees 32 per cent, while the centre is the lowest at 29 per cent.

This means that Isak is better off simply staying central, occupying defenders as opportunities for crosses are more likely to arrive.

So, the question truly is: would you rather a striker be involved in games, but get fewer goals, or have limited touches but still impact matches with his finishing?

Mikel Arteta admits Arsenal are struggling with an old problem that became so cliched that it was featured in a sit-com 18 years ago.

The Gunners beat Hull City 1-0 on Saturday in the Premier League, with Martin Odegaard scoring the only goal at the Emirates.

Any problem Arsenal are struggling with is not too serious as that win, followed by Manchester City’s defeat at Nottingham Forest, put Arteta’s men six points clear at the top of the table.

However, Arteta was frustrated with Arsenal only scoring one goal and it not coming until the 72nd minute, despite dominating possession and producing 21 shots at goal.

Sometimes the inability to even produce a shot was the problem, despite having the ball in dangerous areas plenty of times.

In a 2008 episode of The IT Crowd, Moss and Roy both try to ingratiate with football fans by learning the phrase: ‘The thing about Arsenal is they’re always trying to walk it in.’

Arteta seems to have a similar take on his team, accusing them of trying to score the ‘perfect goal’ against defensively-minded teams.

‘[We need to] be more efficient,’ the Arsenal manager said. ‘We are one against one against the keeper. That’s happened twice today. There is a penalty there, there is another situation inside the box where the ball is bouncing.

Odegaard is Arsenal’s top-scorer this season with five goals in all competitions and three in the Premier League.

#2017. 'Severe rowdy' behaviour fears over changes to York City's home ground

Proposals for the LNER Community Stadium include a self-service ‘Box Bar’ to cut queues, reducing its licensed hours, indoor sports matches broadcasts and outdoor events and performances.

An application from the stadium’s operator stated the Box Bar would improve customer service by increasing the points of sale for alcohol which would cut queues at peak times.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

But two objectors who have bought homes in the nearby Castra Park development said they feared the changes would threaten the peace and quiet of the family neighbourhood.

York Council environmental health officer Michael Golightly said the application should be refused on public nuisance grounds as the potential effects of the changes could not be measured.

It comes as Greenwich Leisure Ltd’s (GLL) application is set to go before councillors for a decision on Monday, November 16.

Changes proposed for the stadium, at Huntington’s Monks Cross Shopping Park, include allowing outdoor events including boxing and wrestling matches, live music and other performances.

Plans to host six events a year including three boxing and wrestling matches within the stadium bowl in May and June have been drawn up.

Those plans, lodged by the York Stadium Management Company, are being dealt with under a separate application.

The stadium’s licensed hours would also be reduced from the current 2am to 11.30pm daily.

Sales would still be permitted from 8am across all of the 8,500-capacity stadium’s licensed areas.

Non-sporting events such as showing televised matches on screens would also be permitted.

The venue would also be licensed to hold indoor sporting events and other performances, stage live music and play recorded music.

The stadium would be operational from 6am to midnight every day.

Plans stated the self-service Box Bar will be supervised by at least two members of staff to intervene if issues arise and prevent service to under 18s.

They added the stadium’s licensed areas would be monitored by CCTV at all times and other measures would be in place to manage licensed activities.

The measures, including plans to manage events where 500 or more people are set to attend, have been agreed by operator GLL and North Yorkshire Police.

But a resident who is set to move into Castra Park, which is on land between the stadium complex and Huntington’s New Lane, said they were extremely concerned.

The objector said: “Introducing a fast-service Box Bar designed to increase the speed and volume of alcohol sales, combined with broadcasting non-sporting televised events, will generate a severe public nuisance.

“The resulting noise, shouting, and rowdy crowd dispersal at 11:30pm will cut directly into the peace and quiet of a brand-new residential family neighbourhood.”

Another future Castra Park resident said the roughly 300 new homes at the development would be exposed to late-night noise if the plans go ahead.

They said: “Increasing alcohol availability and extending operational hours will draw larger, less predictable crowds into an area that now borders new residential streets and pedestrian routes.

“This raises legitimate concerns about antisocial behaviour, crowd management, and the safety of residents who will be living within metres of the stadium perimeter.”

#2015. When will Manchester United sack Michael Carrick and who could replace him as manager?

Michael Carrick’s days as Manchester United manager are numbered, according to reports.

The pressure has been mounting on Carrick following a disappointing start to the season, and the situation took a turn for the worse over the weekend as, without kicking a ball, Man Utd slipped into the Premier League relegation zone after Nottingham Forest beat Manchester City.

Man United then fought back from two goals down twice to draw at home with Aston Villa on Sunday, but the result was not enough to climb out of the bottom three.

As previously reported by The Athletic, United hierarchy held talks about Carrick’s future as head coach following the 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth on October 25.

Carrick had been widely expected to be sacked at that point and then again after Man Utd were beaten 2-0 by Chelsea in the Premier League, a result that sent them crashing down the table.

However, it was agreed that Carrick would oversee the Roma and Aston Villa games before his situation would be reassessed prior to the international break.

Now, even though Carrick ended a nine-game run without a victory in thrilling fashion against Roma, the first half performance was a disaster and United could have easily found themselves three or four goals down at half-time.

Of course, the second half did prove that the players are playing for Carrick, so much so that Matheus Cunha went overboard in getting himself sent-off after turning the game on its head with two quickfire goals.

There was the argument that Man Utd picked up some much-needed momentum, but the calamitous fashion of Sunday’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa suggested there was nothing of the sort.

It would appear that United going into the international break in the relegation zone has proven to be the final straw for Carrick as the Athletic reported on Monday night that he is expected to be relieved of his duties.

While it remains to be seen when Carrick’s departure is made official, it is understood that a managerial change is expected before Man United face bitter rivals Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday (November 22).

#2014. Huddersfield Town v Liverpool under-21s: Former Newcastle United keeper eyes career first - plus his two-fold Terriers role

The experienced Huddersfield Town goalkeeper, now 33, has represented ten clubs - in three different countries - and played for England up to under-18 level.

He has seen most things that football has to offer. But not a promotion. Not yet.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It is something that he dearly wants to put right at Huddersfield.

He'd obviously prefer a substantial playing role, but if that doesn't transpire, he will contribute in any way he can.

At League One level, Alnwick has played second fiddle to England under-21 custodian Matty Young so far this term.

The Hexham-born keeper has made two appearances in 2026-27, both in the EFL Trophy and a third will arrive against Liverpool under-21s tonight.

Town's qualification for the next stage of the Trophy is already assured and only a huge away win for Liverpool - which realistically shouldn't happen - will deny Town top spot in Northern Group H.

While the Trophy retains importance, the big priority remains league business.

Alnwick told The Yorkshire Post: "I've played in the Premier League, Championship, League One and in Scotland. I've dotted about a bit on loan at times. But I've never had a promotion, which is something that I want to achieve.

"I've been pushing because I know Matty's playing at the minute.

"The better he does and the better I push him, the more successful the club will be and the more successful I'll be. And obviously I want a promotion as well.

"I think that's not just the squad. I think that's the whole (club) staff.

"And when I say staff, I don't mean immediate staff. I mean all the guys around this place, the ladies who do the food and everything.

"It's about standards. This year I think they have gone up again.

"I think it's a collective thing. It's fans and everybody included who can really push the club to get a promotion."

Approaching his mid-30s, Alnwick - who joined Town on an 18-month deal from Cardiff in January - knows that his role is now two-fold. He has his own job to do in terms of doing everything he can to become No 1.

Equally, he understands that his seniority means that he is also a bit of a mentor for the club's younger keepers.

Especially fellow north-easterner Young, currently on international business with the Young Lions.

He continued: "I love it. For years and years, I've always tried to help the young goalkeepers.

"My aim is to play as many games as physically possible. That still hasn't left me. I still feel like a 21-year-old kid when you ask me if I want to play football.

"But I do also love helping people because I know goalkeeping is a tough world to be in.

"Especially with Matty, he's only 19 years old. I came through at Sunderland until I was 14 years old and then made the move to Newcastle.

"Actually his goalkeeping coach all the way through was also mine when I was a kid. So we've obviously had that connection straight away.

"He's a great lad. And I think he's done well this season. It's different from obviously coming from playing in League Two last season (at Salford) to a big club like this.

"But I think he's handled it really well and I'm helping him, but also trying to push him because it's healthy competition and I think that'll go a long way this season."

Alnwick counts himself fortunate to have learned from some big characters - and not just top keepers - during his grounding at St James' Park.

They include Steve Harper, who spent a loan spell at Huddersfield back in 1997-98.

"I couldn't have had any better and different goalkeepers at the time," he continued.

"When I was really young, Shea Given was coming towards the end, but Steve Harper was still there.

"And then the older ones above me were Tim Krul and Fraser Forster. All of them were really, really different goalkeepers.

"Then Rob Elliot came through as well, who had been and done the lower league stuff and then came to Newcastle.

"So I had a variety of different people to feed off different things because not every goalkeeper is going to be the same.

"I probably modelled myself more on Steve Harper because of the height and his style of play. But it's good to have all those sort of people around you. It's something that sticks with me."

Tonight's game with Liverpool (kick-off 7pm) is the precursor to a 10-day break for Town, who will return to competitive action at home to Leicester City on November 21 - their fourth consecutive match at the Accu Stadium in all competitions.

#2011. Xabi Alonso takes aim at his Chelsea players after shock Sunderland defeat

Xabi Alonso was not looking for excuses after his Chelsea side was beaten 1-0 at Sunderland, admitting they did not defend or attack well enough.

The Black Cats were bottom of the Premier League table with just one win in nine games when they welcomed Chelsea to the Stadium of Light on Sunday afternoon.

The Blues returned to London with nothing, though, with an Enzo Le Fee penalty the difference between the sides.

There was controversy over the penalty decision, with Levi Colwill adjudged to have hauled down Brian Brobbey, although it looked like both players were pulling the shirt of the other.

Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders hit out at the decision, telling Sky Sports: ‘For me it wasn’t a penalty. He barely touched him, I think it was the other way round. He grabbed him.’

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Alonso was not singing from the same hymn sheet, telling the BBC: ‘I haven’t seen it back. Nothing to comment on the referee. It is something that is our fault. We could have done better.’

He added: ‘I think it’s an action where he can defend better. It’s our mistake.’

Alonso was impressed by Brobbey over the game, not just in winning the penalty, but felt his defenders could have done better against the big Dutchman.

‘From transitions out of almost nothing he got a couple of chances, he got the penalty as well,’ he said. ‘But we have been preparing for that, we have tried, we could have done better.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘He is not unstoppable. He is stoppable but when you defend better than we did today.’

Clearly the former Real Madrid boss did not like he saw from his defenders and he was also frustrated with what his forwards produced.

‘I think we didn’t deserve more than probably one point,’ he said. ‘Not much happened, to be honest. We didn’t produce enough to deserve to win.

‘We were against a low block we missed a bit of patience, a bit of quality, a bit of creativity on the last third to create more chances, you need to be more consistent to move the ball from one side to the other that we didn’t do good enough.’

It was suggested to Alonso that Sunderland’s physical superiority meant they could bully Chelsea, but the manager said: ‘Not bullied. There’s situations that we could have defended better. Situations that we could have had better advantages in attack.’

Defeat left Chelsea fifth in the table, while Sunderland climbed to 18th.

#2008. Michael Carrick responds to Man Utd relegation fears after Aston Villa draw

Michael Carrick downplayed fears Manchester United were in a relegation battle after a remarkable 4-4 draw with Aston Villa in the Premier League.

United will sit in the relegation zone of the Premier League during the November international break after a thrilling 4-4 draw with Villa at Old Trafford.

Aston Villa twice led by two goals but Manchester United produced two spirited fightbacks to avoid defeat and potentially prolong Carrick’s reign as manager.

Goals from Brazilian winger Alysson and Senegal striker Nicolas Jackson put Villa 2-0 up inside five minutes but the hosts were level by half-time thanks to Bruno Fernandes’ penalty and Youri Tielemans equaliser against his former club.

John McGinn restored Aston Villa’s lead just after half-time and the visitors appeared to have the game wrapped up when Leon Goretzka scored a fourth on 53 minutes.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But injury-time goals from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu saw Manchester United salvage a point and avoid a third successive league defeat.

The comeback rivalled the one United produced in the Champions League against Roma during the week but it remains to be seen whether it saves Carrick his job.

Despite avoiding defeat, the Red Devils slip to 18th in the Premier League after ten games, their lowest position at the stage of a campaign since 1986.

Carrick’s side have also gone eight league games without a win, matching a run they have endured just once before in the Premier League.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I’m disappointed that we haven’t won the game,’ Carrick said. ‘We looked the better team for long parts of it and we’re making it difficult for ourselves with the goals that we’re giving away.

‘We’re not just giving away one, it’s two in succession that put us in such a difficult position. We did it the other night, we did it again today and have come back into the game and had a lot of the game, could have won it at the end.

‘So I’m disappointed we haven’t won the game. It’s just moments that we need to tighten up on. Individual moments where we’re giving teams goals that we don’t normally get.

‘If we tighten up that, there’s a lot of good in that performance. I thought we should have won the game. But conceding the goals we are is not helping us at all.

"That's not going to happen" 🗣️Michael Carrick responds to the notion that he could resign as Manchester United head coach 🔴 pic.twitter.com/q1fBKSXL7l

‘We have got to tighten up, it’s pretty obvious to say that. It’s giving us too much to do in games. But I thought we did a lot and feel that we should have won the game.’

Asked whether he feels Manchester United are in a relegation battle, Carrick added: ‘We’re in November. I don’t like this situation or the results but we can definitely do something about it.’

Responding to Carrick’s post-match interview, former Manchester United captain Roy Keane said: ‘It’s obviously difficult for the manager. He’s under pressure, no doubt

‘He talks a lot but doesn’t say much. I don’t know if that’s a tactic. Like a politician. He keeps saying we need to tighten up and there’s things we need to work on.

‘But they better get moving on that. It’s the worst start in how many years, all these stats aren’t very good. If you keep giving up goals and chances, it’s just going to continue.

‘What are we expecting to change over the next few weeks and months? What are they working on? They need to do a lot better than that.’

While Manchester United slipped into the relegation zone, Aston Villa stay 10th after extending their unbeaten league run to seven games.

Man Utd’s interest in the Argentine head coach dates as far back as 2016, with Pochettino even meeting Sir Alex Ferguson for dinner while in charge at Spurs.

In May of this year, Pochettino revealed the Red Devils’ interest was more than just rumours. He told FourFourTwo: “United have always shown interest. But the ideal scenario to manage there has never quite materialised.”

He continued: “In any case, that lunch with Sir Alex had absolutely nothing to do with it.

He explained: “I was under contract at PSG.

“After our Champions League elimination against Real Madrid, we had no option but to make sure we secured the Ligue 1 title at least.

“United were in a hurry to announce their new manager before the end of that season because the situation had become unsustainable. I couldn’t negotiate, whereas Ajax gave Ten Hag the flexibility to do so.”

The former Southampton manager also told L’Equipe earlier this year that he would relish a chance to return to the Premier League.

‘When they were on a good run of results last year, the goalkeeper was doing very well, making a lot of big saves, he’s not doing that. Bruno was on fire, he’s not at his very best at the moment.

‘The goalkeeper has to do better. It doesn’t help if your goalkeeper isn’t making saves, that hurts the team a lot.

‘So there are some basic footballing reasons… but to be in the bottom three, playing for Man Utd… this should be hurting them.’

Following the November international break, Manchester United return to action with a daunting trip to Anfield to face arch-rivals Liverpool.

Aston Villa, meanwhile, who stay 10th after twice blowing a two-goal lead at Old Trafford, face relegation battlers Sunderland next.

#2005. Maxim De Cuyper's telling response to Brighton title talk on social media and Diego Gomez's classy gesture

Maxim De Cuyper said high-flying Brighton will stay humble amid growing title talk.

The Seagulls have enjoyed a blistering start to the season and Sunday's 2-0 win against Brentford places them second in the table as they pause in the international break.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Arsenal lead the way at the top, five points ahead of Brighton, with Manchester City one point adrift of the Seagulls in third.

De Cuyper, 25, has been a key man for Fabian Hurzeler and the left winger has started all 10 Premier League matches with two goals and three assists. He has four goals and four assists in all competitions.

"It's impossible to not see those kinds of things if you have social media yourself,” said De Cuyper after the win against Brentford.

"The only thing we say to each other is that everyone has to stay humble and do his job 100 per cent.

"It's going pretty well. Yeah, very good start. Like we said already some weeks ago, it's about us. We have to do the basics right and everything is possible then."

Brighton have 22 points from 10 matches and are the top scorers in the division with 26 goals. They have won seven, drawn once with their only two losses away Liverpool and Chelsea.

The Belgian added: "It obviously makes it easier when you win games to do this effort over and over again.

"You know what you're doing right and you just keep on doing those things that have got you the results.

"But we said it already to each other, if things are going not in our way, we still have to keep on doing it and in the season you have difficult moments so we will definitely meet them and then we have to show how strong we are as a team."

De Cuyper also gave special praise to his teammate Diego Gomez. The Paraguayan followed up his remarkable halfway line strike against Crystal Palace with another long range stunner to open the scoring against Brentford.

"For the moment we just have to give him the ball around the 16 [penalty area] and he will shoot balls into the net." De Cuyper said. "So it's unbelievable for the goals he's scoring this season so I hope it keeps on coming."

Brighton, along with the rest of the Premier League, now pause for the international break and resume Premier League action on November 22 at Hully City.

De Cuyper teams up with Belgium as they travel to Turkey on Thursday, November 12 in the Nations League. They then welcome Italy - also in the Nations League - on Sunday November 15.

De Cuyper said: "It's a nice mental break now. Yeah for sure it's nice to see people from your own country.

"Also some friends and to speak your own language. It's very nice to go back to the national team, have a great time, have some playing time there and then come back with a good mood to go on in the league."

#2004. Gary Neville names four players who will ‘get Man Utd relegated’ after Aston Villa draw

Gary Neville has slammed Manchester United’s failure to sign any new defenders last summer and says the back-four that finished the remarkable 4-4 draw with Aston Villa will ‘get the club relegated’.

The Premier League giants go into the November international break sitting 18th in the table after Villa twice blew two-goal leads to draw at Old Trafford.

United found themselves 2-0 down inside five minutes as Alysson and Nicolas Jackson took advantage of the hosts’ fragile defence.

Michael Carrick’s side were level at half-time thanks to Bruno Fernandes’ penalty and Youri Tielemans’ 44th-minute strike against the club he left last summer

Josh McGinn restored Aston Villa’s lead with a penalty straight after the interval and the visitors looked on course for a big win when Leon Goretzka scored a fourth.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But Manchester United scored twice in injury-time – substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu with the goals – to salvage a point and avoid sitting joint-bottom during the international break.

Despite two comebacks, United’s current position is their lowest at this stage of a season since 1986, while their eight-game winless league run has only happened once before.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Manchester United finished the Aston Villa thriller with a back-four of Noussair Mazraoui, Leny Yoro, Ayden Heaven and Patrick Dorgu, and Neville said that line-up would struggle to avoid relegation to the Championship.

‘The reason Manchester United have conceded four goals is because they haven’t invested in the defence in the transfer window,’ he said on NBC Sports.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Every one knew they had to do that, they needed defenders. The current ones are making mistake after mistake after mistake.

‘The defenders that finished that game will get you relegated. Watch the defensive errors… we all screamed in the transfer window that they have to bring some defenders in.

‘They had to bring the transfer budget forward and bring defenders in.’

Gary’s brother Phil, who also enjoyed incredible success at Manchester United as a player, added: ‘The back-four that finished the game – Mazraoui, Yoro, Heaven and Dorgu – that gets you relegated.

"Should be banging heads!" 😡Roy Keane discusses how Manchester United can improve their form pic.twitter.com/r7JZzj62LD

‘That back-four gets you the sack as a manager and that back-four cannot keep United, I don’t think, in the Premier League.

‘That back-four gets you relegated, it’s poor. It’s not good enough to play in the Premier League.’

Despite Manchester United’s grim position in the Premier League, Gary Neville doubts a change in the dugout would improve the situation in the long-term.

‘You can paper over the cracks and get a new manager bounce,’ he added. ‘When the new manager comes in, everybody’s happy for a couple of months and all of a sudden, six months later, it happens again.

‘You can keep changing the manager and thinking that’s going to be the answer. But this has been proven now over eight managers in 12 years, that’s not the answer.

‘Michael could leave, Michael might stay, we don’t know, the ownership don’t have a clue what to do.

‘It’s rinse and repeat. Amorim, Ten Hag, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Carrick, Jose Mourinho, Louis van Gaal, David Moyes, Ralf Rangnick – some of them are world class managers who have had success, there are a lot of promising young managers there, ex players who know the club as well.

‘None of it has worked because if you recruit badly, if you’ve got poor performance department, poor recruitment department, you’ve not got leadership that is strong right through the spine of the football club you will fail.

‘Every organisation in the world will fail if you’ve not got an aligned leadership from top to bottom – your board and your ownership right the way through to the person who is stood on the pitch trying to play football.

‘There are real issues within that football club, you’ve got people doing those jobs who have never done those jobs before in senior positions.’

#2003. Arsenal told new asking price for 'key January transfer target'

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal are expected to explore attacking signings when the transfer window reopens in January, with Antonio Nusa a name prominently linked.

Arteta’s options on the wing were reduced in the last transfer window, with Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli leaving the club.

Greece international Christos Tzolis was brought in from Club Brugge but has struggled with injuries, with the Gunners unsuccessful in their pursuit to add another winger, failing to convince Morgan Rogers or Real Madrid star Vinicius to sign.

Reigning champions, the Gunners sit top of the Premier League but are yet to blow teams away, relying one again on their defensive strength to grind out wins by a single goal.

German newspaper Bild report that Arsenal have already sent scouts to take in Nusa’s recent performances in the Bundesliga.

The 21-year-old had a solid World Cup, helping Norway to reach the quarter finals, and so far this campaign Nusa has scored four goals and set-up a further seven for teammates in nine Bundesliga games.

It is reported that Arsenal previously tracked the winger prior to his move to Germany, Leipzig paying Club Brugge €21m for his services in 2024.

Arsenal’s fellow Londoners Brentford pulled out of a move for the then-teenaged Nusa, their total package worth €37m before doubts over the winger’s back and knees during the medical led to the Bees cancelling the transfer.

Leipzig are said to be reluctant to sell in the winter transfer window, explaining why the Saxony-based outfit have slapped a €80m (£67m) asking price on their asset. This is more than the £50m fee that was mooted recently.

The Gunners have previously made three signings for €80m or more, including summer recruit Bruno Guimaraes. Arsenal paid Newcastle €87.5m (£75m) for the Brazilian, making him the second-most expensive player in Gunners’ history after fellow midfielder Declan Rice, who transferred to north London from West Ham for £105m in 2023.

#2002. Michael Carrick speaks out on Diogo Dalot future after Manchester United fans make feelings clear

Manchester United fans made their frustrations with Diogo Dalot very clear at Old Trafford on Sunday, but Michael Carrick has defended the under-fire full-back.

The bizarre match finished 4-4 with Aston Villa, as the visitors twice relinquished a two-goal lead to their struggling hosts.

Alysson and Nicolas Jackson had put the Villains 2-0 up within five minutes, only for Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans to put the Red Devils level by half-time.

Villa were two goals in front by 53 minutes as John McGinn and Leon Goretzka started the second half brilliantly and Old Trafford was stunned again.

However, Carrick’s men pulled off a remarkable escape in stoppage time as substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dourgu both scored after the 90-minute mark to rescue a point.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Dorgu replaced Dalot on 66 minutes after a nightmare performance from the Portugal international, which included conceding a penalty for felling Alysson, leading to McGinn’s goal from the spot.

When his number came up there were loud cheers from supporters at Old Trafford, which turned to boos as he left the field.

The 27-year-old has played in all 10 of Manchester United’s Premier League fixtures this season but when Carrick was asked if it was time for him to come out of the team, he pushed back and defended the full-back.

‘We’ve got to be careful with that, I think,’ said the Red Devils boss.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I understand the frustration and the disappointment of the supporters. I get it, we’re all frustrated, we’re all disappointed. The players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that.

‘Diogo gives absolutely everything. He’s played in different positions, he’s played really well at times.

‘He gives the penalty away today, he knows that. Maybe he can do a little bit better, alright, that’s part of it, he’s made a mistake.

‘He cares an awful lot and he’s giving everything. I like what he brings to the team, I like what he brings to the group, I like what he brings to the whole environment and the culture that we’ve got.

‘Picking a team and who plays the next game that’s a whole different decision and that’s a whole different game that we’ve got to look forward to now.’

Dalot signed for Manchester United in 2018 and has become something of a symbol of the mediocrity that fans have watched since then.

Gary Neville, who knows plenty about playing full-back for Manchester United, defended Dalot from criticism earlier this year, saying in January on his Sky Sports podcast: ‘He gets a really harsh view at times [from] quite a few United fans. I do think there’s a half-decent full-back in there, and I watch full-backs so closely.

‘I think he’s actually good in the air. I think he’s got good athleticism about him. I think he’s decent on the ball. I don’t think he’s a world-class full-back, but neither was I.’

He added: ‘I think he’s got something about him. I think he’s got 7/10 in him every single week, Dalot, but because we’ve seen him at left wing-back, we’ve seen him at right wing-back, we’ve seen him exposed so many times.

‘I think if he just played right full-back and played there all the time, I wouldn’t be getting rid of him in a hurry.

‘Now, other people might disagree with me, but I think I know the position of full-back, and I think he could do a decent job for Manchester United.’

Neville was not complimentary about the United defence on Sunday, though, saying on NBC Sports: ‘The reason that Manchester United have conceded four goals is they haven’t invested in the defence in the transfer window.

‘Everybody knew they had to invest in the defence. They needed defenders. They’re making mistake after mistake after mistake.’

The draw with Villa means Manchester United have won just one of their opening 10 games of the Premier League season and sit 18th in the table.

#2000. Michael Carrick told Man Utd star was ‘playing for himself’ in Aston Villa draw

Troy Deeney took aim at Amad Diallo following Manchester United’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, claiming the winger ‘flattered to deceive’ and appeared to be ‘playing for himself’.

United twice fought back from two goals down to come away from Old Trafford with a point in Sunday’s thriller at Old Trafford, but the result saw Michael Carrick’s men enter the international break in the relegation zone.

The hosts were punished for their sluggishness early on as Alysson and Nicolas Jackson made it 2-0 inside only four minutes, only for Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans to find the net and draw level.

The Red Devils were once again punished for a slow start, though, as John McGinn converted a 48th-minute penalty before Leon Goretzka capitalised on some calamitous defending from Leny Yoro to restore the visitors’ two-goal cushion.

Staring down the barrel of a fifth Premier League defeat, Carrick rang the changes in search of a route back into the contest in the second half – and it was two of United’s substitutes, Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu, who struck to salvage a draw at the death.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But with his side hovering just one point above rock-bottom Crystal Palace, Carrick will know the scrutiny and speculation surrounding his future is likely to rumble on ahead of the club’s crunch match away to bitter rivals Liverpool in a fortnight’s time.

‘I spoke about this on our last episode on Thursday, I feel like we’re doing the same things with Manchester United,’ ex-Watford and Birmingham striker Deeney said of United’s latest performance on talkSPORT’s Premier League All Access Podcast.

There had been calls for Carrick to field Shea Lacey in place of Amad following the youngster’s outstanding cameo display in United’s midweek Champions League victory over Roma.

However, the United head coach stuck to his guns and kept faith with Amad, who would go on to have a tough afternoon at the Theatre of Dreams.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Amad comes in and flatters to deceive,’ Deeney said of the Ivorian’s display.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘A lot of running into nothing, he was… today it felt like a lot of them were playing for themselves and going, “Look, I’m not the problem!”

‘Amad had about nine shots in the first half that were never going to be on target.’

On United’s problems in the centre of the park, Deeney continued: ‘I saw a midfield that was empty and vacated today.

‘Villa went through that midfield at will, many times in that first 75 minutes.’

Unai Emery made five substitutions before United’s late fightback, with goalscorers McGinn, Alysson, Goretzka and Jackson all removed, as well as the lively Johan Manzambi.

Asked whether the Villa manager had made a mistake with his changes, Deeney replied: ‘Absolutely.

‘I also thought it was one of the few times where he’d probably be very disappointed and would want to go back when you look at taking off Johan Manzambi, who I thought was excellent.

‘His ability to not only roll the player and keep the ball, but buy fouls and take them ten, 15, 20 yards up the pitch was excellent.

‘I think the game got too easy for Villa at 4-2 and I thought Emery started to think a little bit too far ahead, “Okay, I can rest these players”, obviously going away to international break.

‘Nicolas Jackson at times looked like Kylian Mbappe against that Manchester United team. He was dropping team, running in behind, he was 15 yards away from everyone.

‘But I just think he made too many mistakes and you can’t account for a goalkeeper having a shocker as well.’

Diogo Dalot appeared to be targeted with sarcastic cheers from the Old Trafford crowd when he was replaced for Dorgu midway through the second half.

Facing the media shortly after the final whistle, Carrick jumped to Dalot’s defence and encouraged supporters to get behind the players, especially when they are playing out of position.

‘Diogo, he gives absolutely everything,’ Carrick said.

‘He’s played in different positions, he’s played left-back, he’s played really well at times. He gives a penalty away today, that’s, you know, he knows that.

‘Maybe he can do a little bit better, all right, that’s part of it, he’s made a mistake, but he cares an awful lot and he’s giving everything.’

On Dalot, the United boss went on: ‘I like what he brings to the team, I like what he brings to the group, I like what he brings to the whole environment and the culture that we’ve got.

‘Picking a team and who plays the next game, that’s a whole different decision, but it’s a whole different game that we’ve got to look forward to now.’

#1999. Bradford City v York City: Michael Duff on pausing for breath after intense schedule

Following tonight's final EFL Trophy Northern Group C game against York City (7.30pm), the Bantams are inactive for 10 days until Saturday week, when they welcome Doncaster Rovers in a Yorkshire derby in League One.

Duff's side are already through to the next Trophy stage and only a big victory for York – already eliminated – will knock City off top spot.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

In his first three weeks in charge, City had successive midweek games to fit in. But last week's clear Saturday-to-Saturday run and their forthcoming break from action will provide some quality time on the training ground.

Duff, inset, said: "We can get some tactical element into certain things I think we need. We're not trying to change a lot, but the obvious one has been we've got the 'ten' a little bit higher in certain areas of the pitch.

"We introduced a man-to-man press against Oxford, which is something new, so you're just trying to drip a couple of new things in.

"A lot of it will be reinforcing those things, because with the schedule the way it is – and without having a pre-season where you can embed certain fundamentals – it's keeping what you've got and then dripping little bits in. It's just reminders.

"You speak to supporters, they'll probably go 'this needs to change, this needs to change'. Not that much does as it's been going all right, but certain things do need to improve."

Tonight's game is the fourth in a run of six successive fixtures – in four different competitions – at Valley Parade.

Duff added: "It helps with the travel of the players. It might not help if the results don't go so well, but the players know that anyway.

"Supporters are demanding and football drives emotion, I totally get that. They'll all go in the pub and put the world to rights, that's why everyone loves football. That's why they turn up at the weekend – to get the week's worth of venting out. Our job is sometimes you've got to suck it up and swallow it."

While the game is a 'dead-rubber' for York, who make their first competitive visit to Bradford since October 2012, there is one clear motivation with Scott Lindsey's side still waiting to record their first competitive away win since returning to the EFL.

#1998. England XI vs Croatia: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup and injury latest for Nations League

Dan Burn and James Hill have been added to the England squad as replacements for Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa ahead of Thursday’s match against Croatia.

The Three Lions face Croatia at Wembley Stadium in their penultimate Nations League group game, before completing their group-phase in Madrid against world champions Spain on Sunday.

Manchester City centre-back Guehi was assessed over the weekend after being substituted with a hip injury at half time of their defeat to Nottingham Forest but has now pulled out of the squad.

In his place, Thomas Tuchel called up the 34-year-old Newcastle defender. He had said on Friday that “difficult phone calls” had been had with Burn, Dean Henderson and Chelsea’s Jordan Henderson when leaving them behind. But the former is now in as Guehi’s replacement.

Meanwhile, it was announced on Tuesday morning that Konsa will not be available for the Croatia game, but is expected to return to full training later in the week ahead of the Spain fixture.

As such, Tuchel must decide whether to hand Hill a senior debut or reshuffle his defence with Ben White coming in at right-back, thus allowing Jarell Quansah to partner Burn in the middle.

Captain Harry Kane is expected to start and will overtake Peter Shilton to become England’s all-time most-capped player.

Arsenal duo Bukayo Saka (injury) and Noni Madueke (selection decision) are not in the squad this month but the head coach has explained that he sees his options on the right wing as being Liverpool’s Rio Ngumoha, Chelsea’s Morgan Rogers, Nottingham Forest’s Morgan Gibbs-White and Fulham’s Josh King.

Declan Rice is back in the mix and available after missing the last international break due to load management.

Jobe Bellingham of Borussia Dortmund, brother of Real Madrid’s Jude, is in the squad for the very first time at senior level. He, King and the Brighton veteran goalkeeper Jason Steele are the only uncapped players among Tuchel’s squad.

Skipper Rob Hutchings again lined up at left-back with Isaac Bello on the other side, with Ben Pashley and Ryan Davidson in the heart of the defence. Max Evans started between the sticks with Joe Moore, Emmett Dunn, Lucas Pattenden and Worthing loanee Matt Burgess in midfield, behind top scorer Harry Bridle and Brandon Chebby.

The visitors were awarded a free kick in the third minute but Evans collected the resulting header. Then Chebby had a shot of sorts and Bridle turned the loose ball in to put City in front.

Donovan Wilson got Bath’s leveller 11 minutes in before Callum Wood’s corner was headed away by the Chi backline.

Davidson received some lengthy physio treatment just after the half-hour mark and had to be replaced by new boy Will Sweet. It tranpired Davidson had suffered a broken jaw.

Hutchings got done down the right wing by Chamberlain, who pulled a decent save out of Evans.

When Sweet was man-handled by Parsons, and after a melee, referee Joel Lamping consulted his assistant and brandished a straight red.

The visitors changed it up at the break bringing on Reuben Reid, and Bridle had a shot blocked in the first minute of the second half.

The away team thought they had gone ahead moments later through Reid but it was chalked off for offside.

Dunn headed away a corner as the away side pressed once more and Bello’s shot-cross was simple for Richards before Burgess was impeded just outside the penalty area.

Wood delivered one across the danger zone for Bath but no-one was there. A disappointing cross was easy enough for Richards before Pattenden smashed in Chebby’s fine cross on the hour to make it 2-1.

The Chi No19 might have extended the lead following a Pattenden delivery in the 68th minute, and Enzio Boldewijn’s set piece went wide. Then Pattenden’s header was saved spectacularly by Bath keeper Harvey Richards before Bridle blazed one over the bar.

The Somerset side made a triple substitution on 77, and Pattenden tried to lob the Bath keeper but it was easy for him.

Chebby fired a left-footer off target before the ball was turned out for another City corner. Clarke came on for Dunn with five minutes to go and Munt replaced Bridle.

It looked like Richards had handled outside the penalty area as we entered six minutes of additional time. And Chi should have been 3-1 up but Moore somehow missed with practically the last kick.

#1996. Aston Villa chief points finger at Manchester United star after controversial incident

Aston Villa’s Director of Football Operations has hit out at the controversial decision to let Manchester United’s equaliser on Sunday stand.

A thrilling contest at Old Trafford finished 4-4 as the home side scored twice in stoppage time to rescue an unlikely point.

Villa went 2-0 ahead within five minutes thanks to goals from Alysson and Nicolas Jackson, before Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans leveled things up before the break.

The Red Devils started the second half as badly as they did the first as John McGinn scored from the penalty spot before Leon Goretzka made it 4-2 on 53 minutes.

As the clock ticked past 90 minutes it looked bleak for Michael Carrick, but substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu scored in injury time to give the home fans something to cheer.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Dorgu’s headed goal was not without controversy as Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki claimed he was impeded by his opposite number Senne Lammens who was up for the corner.

Manchester United legend Roy Keane did not think it was a foul by the Belgian, saying on Sky Sports: ‘I don’t think Suzuki gives himself the best chance of getting it, he’s underneath it, just take a step back and attack it. There are bodies in the way, but there’s lots going on, football is a contact sport. I have no problem with it.

"Football is a contact sport!" 🗣️Did Senne Lammens foul Zion Suzuki for Man United's equaliser? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/KCb1lHqPHP

‘A goalkeeper in this situation, he should take command of it. If he’s talking about getting blocked and pushed, why doesn’t he do that to the opposition players?

‘He’s got to come and be aggressive. When the ball comes in he’s on his heels. He’s got to be more aggressive and take command of that six-yard box.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The incident will split opinion as Lammens seemed to look at Suzuki, turn his back to him and then purposefully nudge him with no attempt to play the ball.

That was certainly the stance of Damian Vidagany, who says referees had vowed to be harsher on such incidents.

Posting on X, Villa’s Director of Football Operations wrote: ‘To put in context this convenient narrative of “contact sport” we’ve been told by referees during the summer that this season to go to unbalance or push the GK on purpose on the six hard box was not going to be allowed anymore.

‘Lammens not even look at the ball, went straight to do a contact with the hip over Zion.

‘Having said that we played good match and we must do better than last 6 minutes. We will do and we will improve. But the rules are the rules and must be respected. That is a fact.’

Villa boss Unai Emery said his 24-year-old goalkeeper, who arrived from Parma over the summer, is still getting used to Premier League officiating, which is different to elsewhere.

‘When we are conceding the last goal in this corner, it is adaptation,’ he told Sky Sports. ‘Adaptation to the Premier League for Zion to settle here well. He must try to, because it is not the same timing. Here is not foul. They are pushing, they are disturbing the keeper.

‘Of course, in another countries, another leagues, they are not permitting it. Here, yes. We have to continue analysing, having experiences, and trying to avoid situation like we conceded.’

#1995. Derek McInnes will soon have a Rangers selection headache as two-striker approach assessed

Kris Boyd insists Ryan Naderi’s impressive form in front of goal has provided Derek McInnes with a selection headache he will be more than happy to have, with the striker stepping up in the absence of key attacking options.

The German forward has seized his opportunity in the starting line-up since club captain Lawrence Shankland and Youssef Chermiti were sidelined through injury, linking up effectively at the top end of the pitch with £9 million summer signing Kevin Kelsy.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The pair have struck up a potent partnership in recent weeks, playing a key part in five successive wins that have provided renewed optimism surrounding Rangers’ title credentials this season.

Former Ibrox marksman Boyd has been impressed by Naderi’s all-round game and development after starting the season well down the pecking order, although he suggests there is still room for improvement.

“There's no doubt Chermiti was going to be the one at the top end of the pitch and maybe Shankland behind him,” Boyd said. “Kelsey has come in and he and Naderi have struck up a partnership.

“Shankland will be back soon. He is different to the other two and I still think he’s the best finisher at the club. But he will have a fight on his hands getting back in the team. It’s a good problem for Rangers to have.

“At the start of the season they were creating opportunities but weren’t taking them. You do feel they can score goals, but, more importantly, this team has more of a McInnes DNA defensively. Back then they had to score two, three or four goals to win a game. Right now they can get by with a 1-0. You’d want to kill it off a lot quicker than they do, but it was another three points [on Saturday] and defensively very good.”

Boyd is an advocate of McInnes' decision to play with two strikers, having operated in that system throughout his own career. He believes the approach provides Rangers with a greater physical presence and gives the opposition more to think about.

“Overall, both of them [Kelsy and Naderi] bring so much to the team and the way Derek wants to play. He wants to get the ball forward and it's two big boys who will ask questions of defenders. Both of them have been scoring. If you wanted to ask for more it would be goals from the wider areas.

“I played that way all my career but football has changed. Derek has always wanted to have two strikers though. Even when they were struggling at Kilmarnock he’d go two up top with wingers. I do think if you are one of the best sides in the country, you can have two strikers on the pitch as long as everyone is doing their work.”

The title race remains finely balanced heading into the final international break of the year, with Celtic four points ahead despite Rangers having a game in hand.

Boyd believes McInnes will welcome the opportunity to take stock of his team’s progress, even if they have continued to find ways to collect points.

“I don’t think he will be upset about the timing of the break,” he said. “Football is about momentum but you do need that break or reset to remind the players about the run they’ve been on. You always feel the last international break to the one in the New Year is when the league starts to sort itself out. Derek will want them refreshed to kick on towards the festive period.”
