#1942. 'I'm a little disappointed' - Jaka Bijol makes candid admission over lack of Leeds United action

Jaka Bijol has conceded he is “a little bit disappointed” with his lack of action at Leeds United.

The 27-year-old defender arrived at Elland Road from Udinese in the summer of 2025 and was a key figure as the Whites avoided relegation from the Premier League last term.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He has not been quite as influential this term, managing just three league starts. Whites boss Daniel Farke has had to do without Joe Rodon of late yet £15m acquisition Bijol has remained on the periphery, with the manager preferring to deploy Tarik Muharemović, Nico Elvedi and James Justin in his three-man defence.

Bijol, who is now away on international duty with Slovenia, told 24ur: “The situation is a bit different than last season. I'm sure I've shown enough this year, so I'm a little disappointed with the whole thing. But that's how it is, you have to accept it.

“Every footballer who doesn't play is unhappy. These are facts and I would be lying if I said anything different. On the other hand, I know that the club is doing well. I'm also happy about that, because this is an exceptional club with exceptional fans who deserve good results.

"I also have to have the right attitude and be right in training. It can happen that everything changes overnight and you're playing the next day. That's when you have to be ready to put in a good performance.”

Rodon is now back from injury and made his return from the bench in Leeds’ 1-0 win over Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday (November 7).

Bijol may now be the the fifth-choice option and with Leeds’ central defenders in strong form, a pecking order change does not appear imminent.

He said: “In football, you really depend a lot on one person, but that's just the way it is. You have to keep going and working.

“I've always believed that the effort in training and putting everything into your work pays off in the end. So far, this has always happened and I believe it will this time too. Keep your head up and keep working.”

Slovenia will host Switzerland on Friday (November 13) before visiting North Macedonia on Monday (November 16). His club teammate Elvedi could be among those he faces in the meeting with Switzerland.

#1940. Ben White: England legend demands 'lifetime ban' for Arsenal star after squad snub

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Chris Waddle has called for a “lifetime ban” for Ben White after the Arsenal defender’s previous refusal to represent England.

White ended a self-imposed exile from the England national set-up in March 2026 when he accepted a call-up from boss Thomas Tuchel, featuring in friendlies against Japan and Uruguay.

Before that, White had not represented his country since the 2022 World Cup, quitting the tournament shortly before the end of the group stage for ‘personal reasons’.

It has been suggested that White’s refusal to play for England stemmed from a ‘barbed comment’ made by then-assistant manager Steve Holland, with former Three Lions manager Gareth Southgate reiterating that he would call-up the Arsenal defender if he was available for selection.

Waddle, capped 62 times by his country, believes that White should never have been given the chance to play for England again.

Speaking to iGaming.com, Waddle stated: “Listen, Ben White shouldn’t be in the England squad, that’s my opinion.

“He refused to represent his country. I'm surprised Thomas (Tuchel) brought him back in, and I don't get why he has. There might be a shortage of fullbacks, but when somebody turns down playing for their country, like Ben White did at Euro 2024, to me that's a lifetime ban.

“I'd say, ‘Forget it mate, on my watch you're not getting back in.’”

The former Tottenham midfielder said he would go one step further, permanently marking White’s England record after his refusal to accept a call-up.

Waddle added: “Once you turn your country down, there should be an asterisk next to your name that means you will never get the opportunity to put on that England shirt again. End of story.”

White has been included in the Three Lions’ squad to face Croatia and Spain in the Nations League, prompting discourse about his refusal to play for England under Gareth Southgate.

Jordan Henderson in March stated that Three Lions internationals ‘would always support’ White, while manager Tuchel has described his decision to recall the defender to the fold as a ‘new chapter’.

#1939. Moretto: Krösche ‘continues to push’ to bring Hardung with him to Milan – the situation

Matteo Moretto has confirmed that Markus Krösche will look to try and bring Timmo Hardung with him to AC Milan.

In the past few days, there have been reports from a number of sources claiming that Gerry Cardinale is finally going to get the man that he has wanted for a few months. Krösche – who left Eintracht Frankfurt last month – has an agreement in place to come in and lead the management.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The issue of the compensation to be paid to Eintracht seems to have been resolved, so now the main question concerns whether someone will come in to help him as a sporting director, another position vacant in the current set-up.

In a video on their YouTube channel, Fabrizio Romano and Matteo Moretto gave some updates on the plans for Milan moving forward, including the restructuring of the management. MilanNews relayed the words of the latter.

“The Krosche deal has been a rollercoaster ride. AC Milan had practically already finalised the deal before the summer window. It was also a question of timing and also of finances, as Eintracht Frankfurt were asking for much higher compensation than what Milan has paid so far, or will soon pay,” he said.

“Anyway, here we go: Marcus Krösche will be ​​Milan’s new Head of Football. Milan will pay compensation of between €3-4m. Official confirmation, as far as I know, will arrive in early January. However, it’s clear that Krosche will already begin working behind the scenes for AC Milan in the coming months, and then he will officially be the new Rossoneri director from January.

“Krösche fits into an organisational and sporting structure that Cardinale had already thought of once he had restructured Milan from scratch. There are other figures within the Milan structure, such as Bobby Gardiner, Almstadt, who from what I understand will remain, but it is clear that Krosche’s figure will be predominant and on a sporting level he will be the one with the most power.

“From what I understand, Krösche continues to push to try to bring in a sporting director who can add to the organisational chart and the name that continues to buzz in Krösche’s head is certainly that of his right-hand man Timmo Hardung, who is the current sporting director of Eintracht. However, it is still to be seen whether Timo Hardung will remain at Eintracht 100%.

“It is true that Eintracht are trying to give him as much power as possible, but I do not rule out Hardung’s exit starting from January or February. Milan remain on the lookout, other German clubs such as Nürnberg, Hannover or Hamburg are also interested in Hardung. Milan wants try inserting another figure, maybe a little further forward.”

#1938. Bradford City 4 York City 0: Clean EFL Trophy sweep for Bantams who show ruthless side again

BD8 was packed to the rafters just 10 days earlier for Bradford City’s juicy league meeting with Huddersfield Town.

On this occasion, in front of an understandably sparse crowd, the atmosphere was low octane in comparison.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

For those that ventured out, including a decent-sized following of almost 700 supporters from the walled city - with York making their first visit to this part of West Yorkshire since October 2012 - it proved worth their while, even if there was little riding on this final Northern Group C game.

Bradford were through, most likely as group winners unless something silly happened. Which it definitely didn’t.

A first-half opener from returning captain Antoni Sarcevic - whose three goals this term have all been on home soil - put the hosts on their way to a clean sweep of group victories.

A third cup strike of the campaign for Stephen Humphrys rubber-stamped the win before another striker with a penchant for goals in knock-out football this season in Will Swan provided gloss.

Swan’s 70th-minute strike, nine minutes after Humphrys’ goal, took his season’s goal tally to seven, with just one in the league.

Substitute Nick Powell joined in the goalscoring action before the end after his midweek brace in the cup against Marine. He is now one shy of double figures.

It was a rewarding night for Michael Duff’s side, whose next two fixtures arrive against White Rose visitors in the shape of Doncaster Rovers and Barnsley. This was a decent warm-up.

With the pressure maybe off a touch, both sets of players among much-changed line-ups, showed good things for the first hour, more especially those in claret and amber.

York’s wait for a first away win on their league return goes on, as does their run without a victory in Bradford - the Minstermen last won here in March 1980.

For 60 minutes, they gave a good account of themselves before the Bantams showed the ruthless edge which mauled Marine. The scoreline was cruel on them on the night.

City made ten changes from their handsome cup slaying of Marine, with Kieran Morgan being the only player who lined up against the Merseysiders.

It was a notable night for Iraq under-23 goalkeeper Zac Hadi, handed a Bantams debut, while Harry Ibbitson started for the first time at Valley Parade.

Fresh from his one-match suspension, Sarcevic got a run-out for the hosts, inactive after this fixture until November 21.

Unlike the Bantams, York were mindful of forthcoming weekend league business at Rochdale. Scott Lindsey not only changed his entire XI from the weekend cup victory over Northampton Town, but gave them the complete night off with none on the bench either.

The Minstermen gave a debut to youngster Lewis Beadle, with keeper George Sykes-Kenworthy getting the nod in goal at the club where he started out.

Bradford led at the break, but both sides contributed to a very watchable contest, more especially given that it was a ‘dead rubber’.

The Bantams and their visitors both hit the woodwork. York played some neat passing football at times, but it was the hosts who drew first blood with an elegant 32nd-minute opener.

The hosts broke with intent and Swan’s perceptive left-wing cross found Humphreys, who spotted Sarcevic in space and found him with a lovely weighted pass and the home captain finished clinically, low past Sykes-Kenworthy - as befitting a goalscoring midfielder of his ilk. It was a quality move and finish.

Humphreys and Sarcevic had some fun in the final period of the half and had further chances, with York starting to look a bit wary. They had brought offerings to the table before that at the other end.

Hadi was forced into significant work to make a strong double save to deny Jovan Malcolm and Joe Grey before producing a textbook parry - and positioning - to keep out Dipo Akinyemi’s goalbound header.

Earlier, York knocked on wood from close range, courtesy of Ethan Shiver. As did Bradford earlier, with Kieran Morgan displaying sublime technique to warm up a nippy November night. His exquisite shot with the outside of his foot clipped the post.

Half-time came at a more convenient juncture for York than the hosts. But it was Bradford who carried on from where they left off ahead of the interval, with Morgan - having a handy game - finding Swan, whose rasping shot stung the palms of Sykes-Kenworthy.

The York custodian was then called into action again to beat out Humphrys’ angled drive, with Sarcevic’s follow-up header hitting the underside of the bar.

In keeping with an entertaining evening, York should have levelled moments later.

Malcolm broke away and went for glory instead of slotting in Akinyemi. Hadi, in keeping with his good night, made himself big and made the point-blank save.

It’s importance was soon magnified when Humphreys’ header doubled the hosts lead just after the hour mark following Reece Welsh’s right-wing centre.

It was Humphrys' last involvement of the night.

Swan tucked home a third following substitute Powell’s cross after the Minstermen were opened up.

City gave debuts off the bench in the final quarter to two youngsters in Leeroy Gomes, Gabe Holt and Oliver Hewitt.

Powell added an effortless late fourth after clever play by the impressive Morgan. A rewarding night for Bradford.

Bradford City: Hadi; Welch, Matthews, Pratt (Hewitt 85); Ibbitson, Cartwright, Morgan, O'Keeffe (Holt 77); Sarcevic (Lunn 62), Swan (Gomes 77); Humphrys (Powell 62). Substitutes unused: Doyle, Gillesphey.

York City: Sykes-Kenworthy; J Hunt, Beadle, Medley (Belleh 62); King, Maguire, Stiver, Grey (Farrar 62), Newby; Malcolm, Akinyemi. Substitutes unused: White, Swansbury, Ozisik, Penrose, Appleyard.

#1937. New Manchester United manager hint dropped amid 'Mauricio Pochettino U-turn'

Manchester United could well be moving towards appointing a new manager.

The Red Devils look set to part company with under-fire head coach Michael Carrick this week, according to widespread reports, with a crisis meeting set to be held in Monaco on Wednesday with club executives including Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox.

Carrick’s position has come under severe scrutiny after just one win in 11 games in all competitions, and United were almost embarrassed at home against Aston Villa at the weekend, falling behind by two goals twice inside the opening minutes of either half.

It was a game that they roared back to draw, with Patrick Dorgu notching an injury-time equaliser, but the level of the overall performance was again cause for concern, with the 20-time Premier League champions mired in the relegation zone after 10 matches.

A three-strong shortlist looks to have come to the fore in terms of replacements for Carrick, with former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe, ex-Bayern Munich and Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann, and Mauricio Pochettino, currently the head coach of the USA national team, all considered.

Pochettino, formerly of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, has been linked with the Old Trafford hotseat before, and has emerged as a wildcard candidate after not featuring in early reporting of potential managerial targets.

Now, however, in an update given by David Ornstein on The Athletic FC podcast, it appears that the Argentine could well be United’s preferred option, should they be willing to meet the $10million release clause that the former defender has in his USMNT contract.

“Julian Nagelsmann is a name that has been mentioned, but I don’t hear that he’s one Manchester United are looking to pursue,” Ornstein said on Tuesday.

“Eddie Howe has been heavily rumoured, but I don’t hear that he’s one they’re looking to pursue. So, by the process of elimination, you get to someone like Mauricio Pochettino."

Pochettino, now 54, has been previously considered by Ineos for a couple of positions, firstly at Nice, and more recently with United.

“In 2024, When [Erik] ten Hag’s job was on the line, United spoke to Pochettino,” Ornstein continued.

#1934. Mauricio Pochettino to break silence on future as Manchester United given deadline to trigger £7m option

Mauricio Pochettino is expected to address the media this week, though he is likely to be quizzed about links to Manchester United rather than the USMNT’s upcoming fixture.

Pochettino, who signed a contract extension with the national team back in August - taking him through to the 2030 World Cup, is busy preparing for this weekend’s Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti.

However, the build-up to the game has been somewhat disrupted by talk of the Argentine becoming the next Man United manager.

Following United’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, Pochettino - out of nowhere - emerged as the new leading contender to replace Michael Carrick in the Old Trafford hotseat.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss is now the favourite among bookmakers for the job amid reports Man Utd chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox will recommend a managerial change during a scheduled meeting with the Glazer family and minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

While the possibility of Carrick staying on has not yet been ruled out, a final decision may not come until Thursday - around 24 hours before Pochettino’s pre-Haiti press conference.

Unless more clarity is provided before Pochettino sits down in front of the media to fulfil his usual pre-matchday duties for the USMNT, he will almost certainly be asked about the Man Utd job, thus forcing him to break his silence on the matter.

According to The Athletic, there is a buyout clause in Pochettino’s USMT contract worth $10million (£7.44m) which Man Utd can trigger to bring back him to England.

“Every time we sign a contract, it’s to go to the last day of the contract,” Pochettino said in August. “If we sign a four-year contract, we need to think to arrive there. And we signed the contract because we really believe that we are going to be four years there. Because if not, it’s bad.

“If we don’t believe in that process, if we don’t believe in that journey, why (would) we sign four years? Only to be sure that we are going to receive a salary on the end of the month? That is not nice. It’s not the way that we think.

“We really signed that contract because we really believe that we can arrive to the end.”

#1933. Leicester City vs Walsall - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 08 Nov 2026 22:11, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 09:54

Leicester City and Walsall square off on Tuesday evening with the winner guaranteed to progress to the EFL Trophy knockout stages.

Given their superior goal difference, the home side only need to draw this contest to edge out the League Two club.

Although the pressure on Leicester boss Russell Martin has somewhat subsided in recent weeks, he knows that he cannot afford to relax in his position at the King Power Stadium.

Only recording a 4-2 win at National League North side Oxford City in the FA Cup first round served as a reminder of how teams will try to raise their performance against the Foxes and Martin.

Leicester have now won four of their last six games in all competitions, the solitary defeat coming by a 2-1 scoreline at Luton Town.

However, the East Midlands outfit have netted 16 times across that period, while Martin's team remain within seven points of second-placed Stockport County in the League One table.

Martin will view this competition as an opportunity to reach Wembley Stadium, and their 6-1 win over Fulham Under-21s is currently the difference between them and their next opponents.

They hold an 8+ superior goal difference to Walsall, who must leave the King Power Stadium with maximum points to progress further in the tournament.

Despite sitting in third place in the League Two table with just one defeat and 12 goals conceded in 13 matches, Lee Grant's side have lost their way in recent matches.

Grant was bitterly disappointed to witness Walsall suffer a 3-1 defeat at the hands of Newport County in the FA Cup first round on Saturday.

Eight goals have now been conceded in their last three games in all competitions, with their one win during that run coming by a 3-1 scoreline at 23rd-placed Colchester United on October 31.

While Martin is expected to make sweeping changes to his Leicester XI, the likes of Tommy Watson and Admir Bristic are notable names likely to feature.

The latter has already scored three goals from two appearances in this competition.

Martin has revealed that youngster Jayden Joseph will not recover from injury in time for this match.

With Walsall having no game at the weekend, Grant will name a strong XI, albeit still with alterations.

Harrison Burke, James Furlong, Isaac Moore, Reece Smith and Taj Sodje could all be handed opportunities in the starting lineup.

Cornell; Gray, O'Hora, Kangasniemi; Aluko, Page, Neal, McFarlane; Howell;, Watson; Bristic

Wooster; Ahui, Burke, Leak, Furlong; Moore, Sprangler; Simper, Dallas, Smith; Sodje

On the back of their FA Cup exit, Grant will likely name a stronger Walsall XI than initially planned. Nevertheless, Leicester should still have enough quality to edge this contest, potentially by the odd goal in three.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Bayern Munich have confirmed Vincent Kompany has returned to the club's training ground for the first time since collapsing last month.

The former Manchester City defender collapsed during a training session prior to Bayern's Bundesliga win over Freiburg in late October.

It was subsequently confirmed that Kompany was in a stable condition and undergoing tests in hospital, with sporting director Max Eberl saying he could miss "weeks".

Kompany's assistant Aaron Danks took his place on the sideline for five matches, overseeing victories over Freiburg, Magdeburg, Atletico Madrid and Mainz, as well as a draw with Klassiker rivals Borussia Dortmund.

#1931. BK Hacken Women vs Chelsea Women - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 08 Nov 2026 22:15, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 20:39

Chelsea Women will head to Sweden for Tuesday's Women's Champions League clash against BK Hacken Women.

The Blues occupy fourth spot in the league phase, while Hacken head into matchday four in 16th position.

Hacken are competing in the Women's Champions League draw for the first time since 2023-24, when they made it out of the group stage before losing to Paris Saint-Germain in the quarter-finals.

Elena Sadiku's side are competing as the reigning UEFA Women's Europa Cup winners after beating fellow Swedish side Hammarby in last season's final to win the inaugural edition of the competition.

Hacken also beat Hammarby to the 2026 Damallsvenskan title, clinching the silverware with a commanding 4-1 victory earlier this month.

After retaining their league crown, Hacken returned to action with a 1-1 draw against Djurgarden on Friday, extending their unbeaten league run to 18 matches.

They will now turn their focus to the league phase, where they are currently two points adrift of a top-12 spot after taking just one point from their opening three matches.

Hacken are currently the league phase's joint second-lowest scorers with just one goal to their name, although that effort did arrive as a stoppage-time equaliser in their most recent European outing against Paris FC.

Chelsea, meanwhile, are one of four teams yet to lose in the Champions League after collecting seven points from their first three league phase games.

The Blues recorded home victories against Austria Vienna and Roma on either side of a goalless away draw against Lyon, laying the foundation for a serious challenge for a top-four spot.

The 2-0 victory over Roma formed part of a five-game winning run that came to a frustrating end in Saturday's 1-1 draw against Everton in the Women's Super League.

Sandi Baltimore grabbed the opener just shy of the half-hour mark, only for Everton to quickly equalise through a Lucy Bronze own goal.

After failing to find the winner, Chelsea dropped two points behind their title rivals Manchester City, who they will face in a crucial WSL clash on Saturday.

However, first they will travel to Sweden for Tuesday's European fixture, with the visitors searching for a fourth consecutive away win as they look to extend their 14-game unbeaten start to the season.

Nesrin Akgun will feature in the matchday squad after recovering from injury to make her first appearance since August as a substitute on Friday.

Sadiku is expected to keep changes to a minimum, although she may decide to recall central midfielder Pernille Sanvig for the European fixture.

Chelsea star Lauren James will not feature before the international break after sustaining a hamstring injury in the 6-0 win over Charlton.

In addition to James, the Blues are also without the services of defender Naomi Girma and forward Mayra Ramirez.

Veerle Buurman, Lexi Potter, Alyssa Thompson, Sjoeke Nusken and Aggie Beever-Jones are among those who could receive a starting spot if Bompastor opts to freshen up her side for the midweek away trip.

#1930. Amorim offers honest Milan reflection: “We’re not ready, we’re far from being a really strong team”

Ruben Amorim continued the criticism of his AC Milan side after their dismal defeat to Ferencvaros, branding them ‘not ready’ to compete on multiple fronts.

Amorim made the decision to enact six changes to the starting line-up from the team that beat Inter convincingly in the derby at the weekend, but it backfired as his team never got going last night and were well-beaten by the Hungarians.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It is reported that after the game the Portuguese coach gave a long speech to his players about their attitude and effort levels. Milan remain incredibly inconsistent on this front, as they continue to alternate very encouraging performances with disastrous and listless ones.

Amorim laid into his team during an interview with Sky after the final whistle, and then he spoke to the CBS Sports Golazo studio shortly afterwards. The exchange was transcribed by MilanNews.

Yesterday you were talking about identity, about character. Was this the difference?

“Yes, technically, tactically, and above all mentally, they were superior and deserved to win. Today we weren’t ready to play professional football, and I felt it. We need to look within ourselves and do better.”

And in the Champions League the level would be even higher…

“We have to focus on the small details, without thinking about the Champions League or anything like that. We just have to focus on improving the more specific aspects of football: the mentality, the heart, the passion. We have to improve on that.”

What is Ferencvaros’ level in European football, how do you rate them?

“I don’t know, it depends on the opponent, but they’re doing very well. They have four wins in four games, a clear identity, and today they were superior to us.”

What did this match tell you about Milan?

“That we’re not ready. We’re not ready, we’re far from being a really strong team. We have moments, in some games, where we’re really strong, but then we can’t maintain our level, especially mentally. So this game told me and all of us that we’re not ready to be a very strong team.”

During the first half, I noticed you were very energetic on the sidelines, and then it almost seemed like you stopped giving directions. Can you tell there’s a certain lack of understanding within the team and that they’re not playing the way you’d like?

“No, I just do what I feel at the time, and sometimes I don’t do certain things just for show. We didn’t play well, that’s for sure; we had a completely different attitude in the last league game, while today we weren’t mentally prepared to fight for the win, and that’s what we need to work on.”

If there hadn’t been the derby at the weekend, do you think this match would have gone better?

“I have no idea, it doesn’t matter. It doesn’t matter, we have to be ready to play every three days in different competitions. So it doesn’t matter if we had a match before or not. I think we have to improve a lot in all aspects of the game.”

Torriani played his first match as a starter. How do you rate his performance today?

“I think he did well in the first half. He had a difficult time with a pass, but Lorenzo doesn’t bear any responsibility for the team’s performance. In fact, in the first half he gave us time to try to make some changes in the second half. So Lorenzo just has to keep working. We have to improve as a team to be stronger.”

#1929. ‘It didn’t sit very well’ – Baena admits Alvarez transfer request irked Atleti team-mates

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Atletico Madrid midfielder Alex Baena admits Julian Alvarez's attempts to join Barcelona this summer "annoyed" the rest of Diego Simeone's squad.

Alvarez was at the heart of one of the most high-profile sagas during the summer transfer window, after saying it was his "dream" to join Barca.

Barca president Joan Laporta was not shy about the club's desire to acquire the former World Cup winner, but the Atleti hierarchy responded by saying they would never do a deal with their domestic rivals.

Ultimately, Alvarez stayed put, with Barca moving for Gabriel Jesus at the end of the window, to provide competition for Raphinha, Lamine Yamal, Fermin Lopez, Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi.

The Argentine's return to the fold saw him booed by his own fans during a draw with Villarreal in August, but he has since been fully reintegrated by head coach Diego Simeone.

Yet Baena said the way Alvarez approached the speculation did not earn him much support in Atleti's dressing room.

"It feels a bit strange when a team-mate says publicly that he wants to leave," the Spain international said in an interview with Cadena SER.

"I can understand a player having doubts if a club like Barca or Real Madrid comes in for you, but, ultimately, it was the way he went about it that really annoyed us at Atletico."

Reporting for duty with @SEFutbol  https://t.co/WUkeGwGcHr

— Atlético de Madrid (@atletienglish) November 10, 2026

Now, though, Baena says all has been forgiven and Alvarez deserves to be supported by everyone at the club.

"We would have supported him regardless of what he decided to do," Baena added.

"The important thing is that he is with us now, and we need to show him all the affection in the world."

Alvarez has netted just twice in all competitions this season while providing three assists, having teed up Giuliano Simeone's opening goal in Sunday's 2-1 defeat to Barca.

Alvarez led all Atletico players for shots (four), touches in the opposition box (seven) and successful dribbles (three) in that game, while also creating two chances.

Atletico's defeat snapped their seven-game winning run in LaLiga. They sit third in the table, two points behind second-place Real Madrid and five adrift of leaders Barca.

Alvarez could feature for Argentina during the international break, as they face Uruguay and Costa Rica in friendlies, while Baena and his Spain team-mates will take on Czechia and England in the Nations League.

#1928. Bromley vs MK Dons - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 08 Nov 2026 22:43

In search of a first win as Bromley manager, Karl Robinson will lead his side into an EFL Trophy contest against former club MK Dons on Tuesday.

MK Dons sit at the top of the group after two games with their place in the knockout rounds confirmed, while their hosts are unable to progress but will still hope to end a winless run.

Bromley will play their second game under the new management of Karl Robinson on Tuesday as they look to get back to winning ways in the midst of a tough spell.

After a memorable 2025-26 in which they won promotion to League One for the first time in their history, they have struggled early in the new term, sitting bottom of the third tier having earned just nine points from their 13 games and winning just two of those while conceding a league-high 33 goals.

That has come alongside back-to-back EFL Trophy defeats for the Ravens at the hands of Brentford Under-21s and Crawley Town, and they also fell short in the FA Cup at the weekend, dropping out in the first round at the hands of fourth-tier Rotherham United.

Their winless run now stands at nine games, including eight defeats, with popular manager Andy Woodman departing in that time, Byron Webster's caretaker spell unable to end their struggles and Robinson's first game in the dugout ending in that first-round defeat.

Now keen to bounce back from that 2-0 cup loss, despite being unable to advance from their EFL Trophy group, Bromley will hope to use Tuesday's game to get up and running under the new boss and build confidence for upcoming league outings.

They meet a fellow League One team in a different position, having already progressed in this competition while building momentum on all fronts in recent weeks.

MK Dons won promotion to the third tier alongside Bromley last season and endured a slow start, but thanks to an upturn in form they now sit 12 on 18 points from 13 games having only lost three of those.

Paul Warne's side have now won seven of their last nine games in all competitions, beginning with consecutive EFL Trophy victories to top the group as they beat Crawley Town and Brentford Under-21s 4-1 and 7-1 respectively.

They headed into the weekend's FA Cup tie on the back of three straight league wins, across which they scored 11 goals, and got past Swindon Athletic to book their second-round spot with Marvin Ekpiteta and Aaron Collins scoring early.

Now on four consecutive victories and with their place in the next round cemented, MK Dons make the trip on Tuesday with the hopes of keeping building momentum with another victory to end the group stage with a perfect record.

While they are out of the competition, Robinson should field a strong Bromley XI as they look to end a winless run and rebuild confidence.

Ashley Charles remains out injured, but Shamal George was able to return between the sticks against Rotherham, while defender Adam Jackson missed out at the weekend after being forced off in the league game prior.

Richard Taylor may again join Kamarl Grant at the back in Jackson's absence, while Mitch Pinnock and Ethon Archer will compete for spots out wide after Mickel Miller, Jodi Jones and JJ McKiernan supported front man Michael Cheek on Saturday.

MK Dons may take the chance to rotate after a busy and productive run of games, and Warne has a deep and strong squad to utilise and allow rests for key men.

They will likely remain without Ryan Barnett, Kane Wilson and Rushian Hepburn-Murphy due to ongoing injuries.

Star forward Aaron Collins will likely sit out, having scored seven goals in the last three games, as may Alex Gilbey, with the likes of Ben Wiles, Daniel Barlaser, Callum Paterson and Ibrahim Fullah able to come in from the outset.

George; Ifill, Grant, Taylor, Mendy; Saville, Conteh; Archer, McKiernan, Pinnock; Cheek

MacGillivray; Jones, Nelson, Sanders; Silvera, Barlaser, Matete, Wiles, Bramall; Fullah, Paterson

Bromley may come into Tuesday's meeting with more to play for in their bid to improve their fortunes this season, but the visitors have an abundance of quality and momentum on their side, and we fancy them, even with rotations, to come out on top away from home.

#1927. Cole Palmer has already issued Mauricio Pochettino verdict amid £90m Chelsea to Man United transfer theory

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Cole Palmer has previously heaped praise on Mauricio Pochettino, amid a transfer theory involving the Chelsea star.

Pochettino was at Chelsea when Palmer was signed in a deal worth £45million from Manchester City on transfer Deadline Day in September 2023.

To this day, there is a strong argument that Palmer played his best club football under the Argentine.

During their one season together, Palmer was the stand-out player in a youthful Chelsea side, leading the scoring charts with 25 goals in 45 appearances across all competitions.

That form led to Palmer being named Men's Young Player of the Year at the 2024 London Football Awards and it was during the ceremony where he spoke about his relationship with Pochettino.

"He speaks to you about anything, like family issues,” Palmer said. “I think if he knows what's going on off the pitch, it can affect how he is with you on the pitch. He's really great at that.

"He's given me the freedom to play my stuff and I like it when he frees you because I feel I can express my stuff more.

"I'm loving it. Every day he's talking to you about different things, not just football things but life things as well. He's good at making you feel good and trying to get the best out of you."

Those Palmer’s comments are rather interesting as one Chelsea supporter, on social media, has predicted a reunion with the Blues No10 and Pochettino at Manchester United next summer.

This comes after the former Blues head coach emerged as the front-runner to become the next Man United manager, with Michael Carrick expected to be relieved of his duties.

On X, formerly Twitter, the user wrote: "If Pochettino takes over at United I can see Cole Palmer being sold for £90m to them next summer."

#1926. Prediction: Italy vs France

Two of European football’s most decorated nations meet at San Siro on Thursday night as Italy host France in a crucial UEFA Nations League clash.

France lead Group A1 with 10 points from four matches, while Italy sit second on seven points. A French victory would guarantee top spot and secure qualification for the knockout stage, while the Azzurri need a positive result to strengthen their own position ahead of a decisive final-day trip to Belgium.

Roberto Mancini’s second spell in charge has produced encouraging signs after an initially difficult start.

Following a disappointing defeat to Belgium, the Azzurri responded impressively with victories over Turkey and a valuable draw away to France. Italy then followed that result with another win against Turkey, moving onto seven points and keeping qualification firmly in their own hands.

Captain Gianluigi Donnarumma was the standout performer in the reverse fixture against France, producing a series of excellent saves to secure a point in Paris. His experience could prove vital again against one of Europe’s most talented attacking units.

There is also growing excitement around Italy’s next generation. Pio Esposito continues to impress at senior level, while newcomers such as Mattia Liberali and Alphadjo Cisse have earned call-ups after strong starts to the season.

However, injuries remain a concern. Giovanni Di Lorenzo, Giacomo Raspadori, Moise Kean and Gianluca Mancini are all unavailable, forcing Mancini to continue reshaping his squad.

France have adapted quickly under Zinedine Zidane, after Didier Deschamps’ reign ended somewhan unceremoniously with the World Cup.

Apart from the draw against Italy, Les Bleus have been flawless in this Nations League campaign, recording victories over Belgium and Turkey to establish a three-point advantage at the top of the group.

Their latest success was especially impressive. Trailing Belgium late in the contest, France produced a devastating spell of attacking football, scoring four times in 15 minutes to transform the match completely.

The visitors possess immense quality throughout the squad, led by captain Kylian Mbappe, who remains the focal point of France’s attack. Marcus Thuram provides another dangerous option, while the return of Aurelien Tchouameni and Ibrahima Konate strengthens the spine of the team.

Defensively, Dayot Upamecano is available again after suspension, though injuries to William Saliba and Pierre Kalulu have reduced Zidane’s options.

France know that victory in Milan would secure first place and remove any pressure ahead of their final group match against Turkey.

Italy’s rebuild under Mancini has generated plenty of optimism, and playing at San Siro should give the Azzurri an additional boost.

However, France appear significantly more complete at this stage – a fully developed team, even if they are playing under a new coach. Their squad depth, attacking quality and growing momentum under Zidane make them arguably the strongest team in the group.

Italy will resist as strongly as possible, particularly with Donnarumma behind them, but France’s superior firepower will likely prove decisive.

There was a lot of clamour for Milan to go out and make an attempt for Tresoldi after his hat-trick against Inter during Club Brugge’s Champions League win at San Siro. The forward grew up a boyhood fan of the club and he has made no secret of it.

Moretto gave an update in a YouTube video on various topics, from the arrival of Markus Krösche to the centre-back pursuit. He also went on to address the idea that a forward could arrive, with his words MilanNews.

“Francesco Camarda’s situation needs to be understood. Milan will certainly have to figure out what to do, they will try to determine the best path for the young Rossoneri striker, who perhaps also needs more playing time,” he said.

#1924. Real Madrid Femenino vs Paris Women - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 08 Nov 2026 23:05, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 02:18

Real Madrid Femenino will welcome Paris Women to the Estadio Alfredo Di Stefano for Tuesday's Women's Champions League clash.

Las Blancas currently sit in ninth spot in the league phase, while Paris FC are hovering just outside the top 12 in 14th position.

Real Madrid are bidding to reach the knockout rounds for the third consecutive season after making back-to-back quarter-final appearances.

The Spanish side are currently inside the top 12 on goal difference after drawing each of their first three matches of the league phase.

Las Blancas played out a 1-1 draw against Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester City, before they spurned a two-goal lead in their most recent UWCL outing against Bayern Munich.

Athenea del Castillo and Lineth Beerensteyn saw their efforts cancelled out by Edna Imade and Momoko Tanikawa in a 2-2 draw in Germany.

That result has formed part of a five-game unbeaten run in all competitions (W3, D2), although Real Madrid were left frustrated by another draw in Saturday's away meeting with Athletic Bilbao, causing them to slip four points behind Liga F leaders Barcelona.

As Pau Quesada's side look to return to winning ways on Tuesday, they should be able to take confidence from the fact they won both of the two legs against Paris FC in last season's knockout playoff round tie.

Meanwhile, Paris FC are dreaming of making the knockout rounds for the first time since embarking on a run to the semi-finals of the 2012-13 competition.

They are currently sitting a point adrift of the top 12 after collecting two points from their opening three league phase games.

Sandrine Soubeyrand's side started their campaign with a heavy 5-2 loss against reigning champions Barcelona, before they fought back from two goals down to rescue a 2-2 draw against Arsenal.

However, missed the chance to build upon that result in their matchday three encounter with Hacken, which saw them drop two points as they conceded a 94th-minute leveller in a frustrating 1-1 draw.

They will at least head to the Spanish capital in a positive mood after cruising to a 5-0 victory in Friday's Premier Ligue clash against Montpellier, extending their unbeaten run to six games in all competitions (W3, D3).

While they have failed to win their last two away games against Real Madrid (W1, D1), they were victorious at the Estadio Alfredo Di Stefano in December 2023, when Gaetane Thiney's penalty proved enough in a 1-0 success.

Lindo Caicedo was forced out with a physical issue in Saturday’s draw with Athletic, sparking fears she could miss Tuesday’s European fixture.

Beerensteyn will be looking to continue her fine run of form after scoring eight goals in her last seven matches for club and country.

As for the visitors, they will be unable to call upon key forward Clara Mateo, who is suspended after being sent off in the closing stages of the draw against Hacken.

Anaele Le Moguedec is set to return to the midfield after dropping down to the bench for Friday’s commanding win over Montpellier.

Evelyne Viens is expected to lead the line, with the striker looking to add to the two goals she has scored in the league phase this season.

#1923. Dejan Kulusevski reveals one-word Zlatan Ibrahimovic message after Tottenham injury return

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Dejan Kulusevski has revealed that he received a message from Zlatan Ibrahimovic when he returned from his injury hell to play for Tottenham once more.

The winger was sidelined for 18 months with a complex knee injury, which he feared would prematurely end his playing career at just 26 years of age.

The Sweden international made his long-anticipated comeback to Premier League action in the dying embers of Spurs’ 1-0 victory over Coventry last month, getting a rousing ovation as he took to the field for the first time in over a year.

Kulusevski has revealed that he received a curt message from his compatriot and former Manchester United striker Zlatan Ibrahimovic after he made his return.

The text simply read “Bravo”, with Kulusevski telling Swedish outlet Footbollskanalen of Ibrahimovic’s key advice during his recovery period, as well as input from another former Tottenham colleague.

“Zlatan and Perisic wanted me to go [visit a doctor in Serbia],” he explained. “I went, and the Serbian doctor was important for me.”

“He said: ‘Don’t think about other operations, this is what we’re going to do.'”

He has since made three more substitute cameos under Roberto De Zerbi, in the victories against Chelsea and Crystal Palace, and most recently in the 1-0 defeat by Leeds at Elland Road last weekend.

Kulusevski had spoken of his disappointment at not receiving a World Cup call-up last summer, with Sweden boss Graham Potter opting against picking one of his most influential players despite admitting that there was a chance that he could have travelled to north America.

Now, however, the former Juventus man is back with his international team-mates for his country’s final two Nations League games this week, as they take on Bosnia and Herzegovina and Poland.

#1922. Chelsea’s Problems Run Deeper Than Joao Pedro’s Injury

Chelsea’s reliance on Joao Pedro has become impossible to ignore. The Brazilian’s absence has coincided with a sharp decline in attacking output, and there is little doubt that Xabi Alonso’s side function better when they have a true focal point leading the line.

Yet reducing Chelsea’s recent struggles to the loss of one player risks oversimplifying a far more complicated situation. The deeper concern is that ten league games into the season, it remains difficult to identify exactly what kind of team Alonso wants Chelsea to become.

Joao Pedro’s value extends far beyond goals. He provides a reference point for the attack, gives Chelsea an outlet when they play directly and creates space for players such as Cole Palmer to operate between the lines.

Joao Pedro is off to a flyer this season 🇧🇷 👏 https://t.co/0YqAx5gJZn

— Premier League (@premierleague) October 11, 2026

Without him, Chelsea have looked considerably less threatening. Attempts to compensate have felt improvised rather than planned. Morgan Rogers and Pedro Neto have both been used through the middle despite neither being a natural centre-forward, while more conventional options have remained largely on the fringes.

That has left the attack looking disconnected. Chelsea’s early-season directness worked because Joao Pedro could receive long passes, hold off defenders and bring others into play. Once that element disappeared, much of the team’s attacking structure disappeared with it.

The uncertainty surrounding the striker position reflects a broader issue.

At various points this season Chelsea have looked like a transition-heavy side willing to attack quickly and accept defensive risks. At other times, Alonso has appeared to move towards a more controlled and possession-based approach.

Neither vision is inherently wrong. What is striking is how often Chelsea seem to move between them.

Formation changes have become frequent, midfield combinations have varied considerably and even the general tempo of the team’s play has fluctuated from week to week. Injuries undoubtedly explain part of that instability, but they do not explain all of it.

The result is a team that has shown promising flashes without yet establishing a clear identity. Supporters can recognise individual ideas, but the overall picture remains difficult to define.

Chelsea’s injury list has been substantial and deserves acknowledgement. Losing key players across the pitch would challenge any squad, particularly when several defensive starters are unavailable simultaneously.

Even so, the underlying numbers suggest there are concerns beyond availability.

The goal tally looks respectable on the surface, but Chelsea’s chance creation numbers are less impressive – something Alonso himself admitted after the defeat to Sunderland, and they continue to concede high-quality opportunities too frequently. This appears to be a team whose performances have not always matched the raw results. Sometimes one way, sometimes the other.

There is also a sense that Chelsea remain caught between phases. Alonso has introduced greater calm around the club and reduced some of the volatility that characterised previous seasons, but stability off the pitch does not automatically produce clarity on it.

Chelsea will almost certainly improve when Joao Pedro returns. His qualities are too important not to make a difference.

The bigger question is whether his return will solve problems or merely disguise them.

At the moment, Chelsea’s season feels less like a story about one injured striker and more like a story about a talented team searching for its identity. Alonso has had encouraging moments and difficult moments in equal measure, and the international break offers an opportunity to establish a clearer direction.

Until that happens, Chelsea will continue to look like a side capable of exciting football one week and frustrating football the next.

#1921. Plymouth Argyle vs Swindon Town - prediction, team news, lineups

By Freddie Cotton | 08 Nov 2026 23:18, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 20:27

Plymouth Argyle welcome Swindon Town to Home Park on Tuesday evening for their third and final EFL Trophy group stage fixture.

In their previous competition outing, the Pilgrims prevailed on penalties after drawing against Newport County at Rodney Parade, while the Robins fell to a 2-0 defeat to the same opposition at the County Ground.

Having been eliminated from the tournament at the quarter-final stage in the 2025-26 campaign, falling to a late 2-1 loss against eventual winners Luton Town, Plymouth will be determined to go one better this season and finish the group stage on a high.

After starting their campaign in emphatic fashion by thumping Crystal Palace U21s 5-1, the Pilgrims could only manage a draw away to Newport, but having claimed victory in the resulting penalty shootout, Tuesday’s hosts picked up two points from their trip to Wales and as a result, confirmed their spot in the knockout stages.

Plymouth have impressed outside of the EFL Trophy too, as after 14 matches Tom Cleverley’s men sit fifth in League One, just three points off the automatic promotion places, while also booking their place in the FA Cup second-round on Saturday afternoon with a thumping 4-0 victory over Southern League Premier Central side Alvechurch at Home Park.

While they only need a draw to rise to the summit of Group 13 on Tuesday evening, the Pilgrims should by no means be underestimating League Two Swindon Town, with the Robins claiming victory in three of their previous four visits to South West Devon.

Following their expulsion from the competition in the 2025-26 campaign, having fielded two ineligible players in their round-of-16 tie with Luton at Kenilworth Road, Swindon will be left extremely disappointed with their efforts in the EFL Trophy this season too.

Despite taking the lead, Ian Holloway’s men began their campaign with a 2-1 home defeat against Crystal Palace Under-21s and, having also lost to Newport at the County Ground just a week later, the Robins can no longer progress to the knockout phase, meaning Tuesday’s match is purely a matter of pride for the visitors.

Unlike their opponents, Swindon are struggling for form elsewhere too, having won just two of their previous nine League Two fixtures to leave them languishing in mid-table, while their FA Cup campaign has already come to an end following a 2-1 first-round defeat to third tier side Milton Keynes Dons.

However, while they find themselves a division below Tuesday’s hosts, the Robins have a particularly good recent record when facing Plymouth, winning two of their previous three matches against the Pilgrims, including an impressive 3-1 win when the sides met at Home Park in October 2021.

Plymouth will be without both Matthew Sorinola and Caleb Watts for Tuesday’s clash as the pair continue their recovery from knee and groin injuries respectively, while Julio Pleguezuelo is a doubt after suffering a calf problem in training last week.

Having been rested against Alvechurch as a precaution, Scottish defender Jack MacKenzie is likely to return to the fold for the Pilgrims this week and so too is Owen Oseni, who featured on the bench on Saturday following a month's absence with an ankle issue.

After missing the entirety of the start of the season, Cleverley also welcomed back Ghanaian midfielder Michael Baidoo in the FA Cup on the weekend and the 27-year-old capped his return with a goal.

Following only his second ever international call up, Swindon will be without Moldovan defender Stephan Negru on Tuesday evening, while Samuel Inwood is also unavailable across the backline with a serious hamstring injury.

Having undergone knee surgery in September, Ben Middlemas continues to be sidelined for the Robins, who will also be missing Ollie Clarke after the 34-year-old sustained a hamstring issue against Barnet a fortnight ago.

Both Paul Glatzel and Anthony Munda remain out for Holloway’s side too with knee problems, and the visitors' injury list is rounded off with Fletcher Holman, who is expected to be back in the new year from a severe hamstring tear.

On a more positive note for Swindon, 20-year-old midfielder Jaylan Pearman returned to the squad against MK Dons from an illness and will be looking to get some more minutes under his belt this week.

Plymouth Argyle possible starting lineup:

Storer; Edwards, Ross, MacKenzie, Rendle; Amaechi, Campbell, Roberts, Pepple; Oseni, Ibrahim

Ward; Debayo, Ball, Kirkman; Griffiths-Brown, Nichols, Butterworth, Clark; Hoare, Hackford, Pearman

Boasting a positive recent record against Plymouth, Swindon will be determined to end their disappointing EFL Trophy campaign on a high this week, while maintaining their impressive streak against the Pilgrims.

However, despite expecting both sides to make changes to their line-ups on Tuesday, we are backing Cleverley’s men to claim all three points and secure top spot in Group 13.

#1919. Rio Ngumoha interview: Liverpool youngster on Chelsea exit, Max Dowman and how Lamine Yamal changed the game

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Rio Ngumoha wears a cheeky smile as he sits in his England puffer jacket at Hotspur Way and discusses his upbringing, his hopes and dreams, and the lasting legacy of a fellow teenager.

Ngumoha, 18, is just a year younger than the Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal and argues: “What he is doing [has] changed football for young players.

“Seeing what he can do so young inspires me and all the other young players in how we can just play freely. The way he plays, it’s like it’s his pitch. It’s a good challenge.”

He has been rewarded for fine form at Liverpool with another England call-up this month, and the absence of Arsenal duo Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke gives Ngumoha a good chance of earning plenty of game time on the right wing against Croatia and Yamal’s Spain.

Tuchel has a glint in his eye whenever he speaks about Ngumoha and from the sidelines when the teen is readying himself to come on, you can tell they share a bond.

“He knows I’m quite talented, which is good,” he says. “Every time I come on he lets me be expressive, be free. I have the belief from him.”

Playing under Tuchel for England and Andoni Iraola for Liverpool are “similar” but their “language is a bit different”, he says, explaining that at England “it is a lot more structured, because you know the manager doesn't have enough time to get his ideas across — so that's why we have a lot more meetings, which is understandable.

“It was definitely difficult at the start when he [Iraola] came in [at Liverpool], but we had to adapt quickly.”

Ngumoha says he has played “a couple of times” against English football’s other talked-about wonderkid, Arsenal’s Max Dowman, but believes he has “played more with him than against him. Max is a top, top, top talent, a top player, and he'll definitely go on to reach many heights. We text each other if [one of us] scores.”

Describing his own playing style as “fearless” is not brash but simply the truth of the matter, and it is this confidence in his ability to go past players that led Tuchel to bring him along for the summer’s pre-World Cup training camp in Florida, handing him his debut, before a call-up for the last international break and another this month.

It was in Florida that he struck up a friendship with Fulham’s Josh King, the pair of them reunited with England this month.

#1916. Man United news: New manager 'favourite' other than Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann amid Michael Carrick sack pressure

By Lewis Nolan | 08 Nov 2026 23:47

Mauricio Pochettino has joined the likes of Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann as favourites to replace Manchester United boss Michael Carrick.

The Red Devils earned a point in their final Premier League game before the start of the international break, with the club drawing 4-4 with Aston Villa on Sunday.

Carrick's side came back from 2-0 and 4-2 deficits to avoid defeat, though the result left the team in 18th place, and their placement has fuelled calls for a change in the dugout.

A number of managers have been linked with Old Trafford, including former Newcastle boss Howe and former Bayern Munich head coach Nagelsmann.

However, the Evening Standard have claimed that current USA national team coach Pochettino has emerged as a leading contender should Carrick lose his job.

Most United supporters will remember Pochettino from his time at Tottenham Hotspur, with the 54-year-old spending five years at the club between 2014 and 2019.

While he failed to win a trophy in London, the Argentine managed to reach the 2014-15 EFL Cup final, as well as the 2018-19 Champions League final, while he guided the club to two third-placed finishes, one second-placed finish and one fourth-placed finish.

It should be noted that Pochettino was dealing with a restricted transfer budget for much of his time at Spurs, yet he created one of the most exciting teams in the division, getting the most out of stars like Harry Kane, Dele Alli, Christian Eriksen and Son Heung-min.

Failed spells at Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea following his exit from Tottenham in 2019 should not overshadow his qualities as a coach, and if he can get the Red Devils to play as energetically as his Spurs side did, then United will be a threat against most opponents.

Even though there may be some concerns about Pochettino's ability to get the club over the line in the biggest moments, United are not in a position to turn down someone with the track record of the Argentine.

No other team have won fewer games in the Premier League this season than United (one), and the club are only one point above last-placed Crystal Palace.

The Red Devils are set for a difficult test against Liverpool at Anfield after the international break, and heading into that game without fundamental changes could be disastrous.

Many fans are fond of Carrick for his contributions as a player at Old Trafford, and perhaps now would be the best time to dismiss him with the chance to walk away after a spirited comeback rather than a potentially devastating result against the Merseysiders.

#1915. McTominay reveals he underwent heart treatment two days before World Cup

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Scott McTominay has revealed he had to receive treatment for an irregular heartbeat before Scotland's opening game at the World Cup in June.

McTominay recently returned to action with Napoli, after being diagnosed with a "mild benign arrhythmia" and undergoing a minor procedure to correct the condition.

The former Manchester United midfielder subsequently missed the first four games of Scotland's Nations League Group B1 campaign, from which they took four points.

He could feature under the Tartan Army's new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli for the first time this month, having returned to the squad for their games against North Macedonia and Switzerland.

And ahead of Friday's meeting with North Macedonia at Hampden Park, McTominay has revealed his heart condition began affecting him five months ago.

"I had to go and get the shock on my heart. It was two days before the Haiti game," McTominay – who then played the full 90 minutes as Scotland started their World Cup campaign with a 1-0 win – said.

"You've prepared so well. I was in such a good condition and then something like that happened. You're thinking, 'how is this happening to me?'

"You have to get on with it; those are the cards that you're dealt in football. Sometimes, things don't go your way.

"I was 100%, and obviously, when you're sat in a hospital bed two days before the first game of the World Cup, about to get put to sleep, it's not ideal, is it?"

He has scored five goals for Napoli since his return to action, with three coming in the Champions League and the other two being a brace in a thrilling 3-3 draw with Roma.

And he now feels back to something approaching his best, saying: "I'm feeling much, much better than I was.

"It was something that needed to be done. In your career, you have moments like that where things can take you by surprise.

"Obviously, it looks a lot worse to people in the media, and family and friends reach out to you after they see news related to a heart issue, but it's a relatively straightforward procedure, which went really, really well in Manchester.

"So, I'm just really happy to be back and playing football again. That's the most important thing in my life and it always will be."

Scotland have lost their last two home matches, both of which have come in the Nations League.

They have not lost three in a row on their own turf since September 2018, while in competitive games they have never previously lost three straight home fixtures.

#1914. Virgil van Dijk issues transfer latest as Liverpool contract expiry looms

Virgil van Dijk maintains that he is relaxed about his Liverpool contract situation.

The Dutchman’s deal at Anfield expires at the end of the current campaign, and there have been no indications so far that he will sign an extension.

The central defender has been one of the Reds’ first-choice players ever since he arrived at Anfield back in 2018, joining from Southampton for £75million.

The No4 has taken on the captain’s armband on Merseyside following Jordan Henderson’s departure, with the 35-year-old racking up 282 appearances for the club since his move.

Now, he has issued an update on his contract status, insisting that he is not panicking over his future.

"I feel good, but it’s not about me at the moment," the centre-back said. "Let’s see. I’m not in any panic whatsoever. I want to keep playing and continue what I’m doing.

"Let’s see what the season brings. I’ve had an amazing time already so far. If that will be extended, that’s the case.

"If not, then I will go somewhere else. There’s nothing to report at the moment, but that doesn’t mean that there’s any stress or anything."

Van Dijk withdrew from the Netherlands’ Nations League camp with an injury - Liverpool confirmed on Monday - and manager Andoni Iraola will be hoping that the issue is minor, meaning that his skipper is able to face Manchester United on November 22.

"Physically I’ve been struggling with a little niggle the last couple of weeks but I do everything in my power to be out there," Van Dijk added.

There are several players that are at risk of slipping down Ruben Amorim’s pecking order with displays like the one against Ferencvaros.

Calciomercato.com write that three clues add up to mean that we can say with certainty that Milan are not aiming to win the Europa League despite being one of the favourites, at least on paper. The defeats against Benfica, Bournemouth and Ferencvaros were determined by two factors.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The first is the attitude of the squad’s key players and the inadequacy of several reserves. The dominant Adrien Rabiot, for example, seems to sink when the Europa League anthem is played. The Frenchman – captain on this occasion due to Mike Maignan’s suspension – wasn’t the only culprit, but was certainly the most obvious.

The thing squad assembled last summer by Gerry Cardinale, Amorim and the management features a strong starting eleven that can compete with anyone (as was the case in the derby), but at the same time lacks alternatives.

In several cases, it’s fair to say that the players aren’t up to the task. Filippo Terracciano’s role is emblematic: already rejected by the previous management, he remained with Milan at Amorim’s request.

His season included 45 poorly played minutes against Benfica before being substituted at half-time, a straight red card as a substitute against Salzburg, and a poor performance against Ferencvaros that drew boos from the crowd.

Doubts are also growing over Ardon Jashari, who – after a few performances that were at least adequate – continues to display obvious technical and tactical limitations. The money spent on him (over €30m) is leading many to run out of patience.

The excellent performances against RB Salzburg and Udinese seemed to have reintroduced a courageous and powerful version of Davide Bartesaghi to Milan, but the most recent test saw him revert to the flaws of last season in terms of personality and concentration.

Pervis Estupinan, on the other hand, seems to have completely disappeared from the radar, having remained on the bench for the entire match against Ferencvaros. The two left-backs have a lot of work to do, and this could influence some transfer choices too.

#1912. Crawley Town vs Brentford U21 - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 09 Nov 2026 00:18, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 05:23

A spot in the EFL Trophy's round of 32 is up for grabs at Broadfield Stadium, when Crawley Town host Brentford U21 for their final showdown in Southern Group H on Tuesday.

The Red Devils are hoping to bounce back after a humiliating FA Cup exit, while the Bees are searching for their third win in four games.

Crawley sacked Colin Kazim-Richards last month, leaving former Leeds United and Sheffield United manager Kevin Blackwell in interim charge until a replacement can be appointed.

The 67-year-old has collected four points from his two league matches in the dugout, drawing 1-1 with Tranmere Rovers before beating Oldham Athletic 1-0 on October 31.

That latest success has seen the Red Devils build up a tally of nine points in League Two, though they remain at the bottom of the table, three points short of 22nd-placed Rotherham United having played two games fewer.

The only negative from Blackwell's tenure to date was the 2-0 FA Cup elimination at the hands of Southern Premier Division South club Wimborne Town on Sunday.

In the EFL Trophy, Crawley sit second in Southern Group H, level on points with their opponents but armed with the knowledge that a draw would likely be enough to see them through to the round of 32, owing to their six-superior goal-difference.

Blackwell's side will be desperate to avoid what would be another demoralising cup exit after seemingly turning a corner in League Two, and they will be buoyed by playing on home turf, where the hosts beat Bromley 4-0 in the EFL Trophy on October 6.

Meanwhile, Sam Saunders's Brentford U21 arrive in commendable form and ready for the challenge of facing senior professionals once again, having won two of their last three outings.

The Bees beat Bournemouth U21 4-3 in a dramatic Premier League 2 showdown on October 26, and built on that triumph with a 2-1 victory over Wycombe Wanderers U21 in the Premier League Cup.

However, Saunders's youngsters were downed 2-0 by Wolverhampton Wanderers U21 on Friday, failing to find the back of the net for the first time in eight games.

That defeat has left Brentford U21 14th in the Premier League 2 table with nine points from seven matches, winning three and losing four of those fixtures, and notably both scoring and conceding 15 goals.

The Bees were hammered 7-1 by group leaders MK Dons last time out in the EFL Trophy, and everyone involved in the club's youth setup will be keen to prevent a second consecutive thrashing in the competition.

Crawley could name a similar lineup to the one that faced Wimborne in the FA Cup, with Danilo Orsi-Dadomo up top, supported by a trio consisting of Stephen Duke-McKenna, Kai Jennings and Dylan Morgan.

Charlie Barker could start at the base of midfield, operating alongside Jude Arthurs just in front of centre-backs Priestley Farquharson and Johnny Russell, with Akinwale Odimayo having undergone surgery on a major injury after being stretchered off in the 2-2 draw against Chesterfield last month.

As for Brentford U21, they will be without senior attacker Fabio Carvalho - who featured in the 1-0 win over Bromley - due to a knock, while 19-year-old striker Kaye Furo is recovering from surgery on a foot injury.

In their absence, Isaac Holland should lead the line, and is likely to be supplied by Ollie Shield, Jacob Hanson and Gustavo Nunes.

Elsewhere, midfielder Antoni Milambo is sidelined after suffering a minor setback following a brief return from his cruciate ligament injury, so Riley Owen and Kiefer Gorman look set to start in the Bees' double pivot.

Mannone; Gordon, Farquharson, Russell, Richards; Barker, Arthurs; Duke-McKenna, Jennings, Morgan; Orsi-Dadomo

Rose; Wheeler-Henry, Avenell, Grey, Picotto; Gorman, Owen; Shield, Hanson, Gustavo Nunes; Holland

Crawley will be optimistic given they are facing a youth side, but fans will be wary after seeing their team stunned by a Southern Premier Division South club in the FA Cup.

Brentford U21 may be fearful after receiving a thrashing last time out in the EFL Trophy, but if the youngsters can settle their nerves, then a narrow win could be on the cards.

#1911. Xavi backs ‘complete player’ De Jong

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Frenkie de Jong is a "complete player" who may sometimes be undervalued by those who do not play alongside him, so says Xavi.

De Jong has been mooted as a potential option to stand in for Virgil van Dijk as captain for the Netherlands' upcoming Nations League games against Greece and Germany.

And on Tuesday, he was a topic of conversation for Netherlands coach Xavi, who also worked with De Jong at Barcelona.

That is after De Jong was played out of position at right-back during the second half of Barca's win over Atletico Madrid on Sunday.

Asked if De Jong's quality is not truly appreciated, Xavi told reporters: "Perhaps among the public, but not among his team-mates.

"If you play with him every day, you end up truly appreciating him. He's a complete player."

It’s training time! https://t.co/lL4eeJY2wg

Of playing at right-back, De Jong said: "Everybody knows I'm a midfielder," in what could be seen as a message to Barca boss Hansi Flick.

"As a player, perhaps you're more likely to feel a bit underestimated."

He told ESPN: "People don't watch matches regularly. Few are those who follow the full 90 minutes. They don't really understand the game, and they don't realise what is happening on the pitch, or why decisions are made.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Christos Tzolis has revealed how Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta is different to any other manager he has played under.

The Greek joined the Gunners last summer in a £34million move from Club Brugge, that saw the winger return to England after a spell at Norwich City.

The forward had an underwhelming period at Carrow Road before moving to Belgium, where he lifted the Pro League title last season, which helped propel him to the Emirates Stadium.

He has just returned from a hamstring injury on international duty that kept him out for a month, but he made a return to action in the 1-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield on November 1.

Tzolis has spoken of his admiration for Arteta being a big part of why he wanted to move to north London, and he explained to Novasports how the Spaniard differed from any head coach he had had previously.

"He does a lot of things before the matches, some alert games, in the locker room to see the players' readiness,” he said.

“He always has different ideas before each game and approaches it differently.

"I mean, I haven't seen that with any other coach. In the first talk we had in the summer, he asked me about my life, about my life outside of the game as well, about football of course.

“And I spoke for 45 minutes, for sure, and 10-15 minutes as coach, so he was very open to hearing what I had to say."

#1909. Inter Milan Women vs Manchester City Women - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 09 Nov 2026 00:29, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 09:52

Manchester City Women will travel to Italy for Tuesday's meeting with Inter Milan Women in the Women's Champions League league phase.

Inter have four points to their name after three matchdays, while Man City are a point worse off after playing out three consecutive draws.

Inter are competing in the main draw for the first time after staging an impressive fightback against two-time European champions Wolfsburg in qualifying.

After losing 2-0 to Wolfsburg in Germany, Inter recorded a 3-1 extra-time victory in the second leg before they held their nerve in the subsequent penalty shootout.

David Sassarini's side went on to take four points from their first two league phase games, edging out Hacken by a 1-0 scoreline on home turf before netting a late equaliser in a 1-1 away draw against Austria Vienna.

However, they failed to take anything from their matchday three encounter against record champions Lyon, conceding six goals without troubling the scorers in their second competitive defeat of the season.

Inter have bounced back from that 6-0 loss with consecutive 3-0 victories in domestic action, including a statement win over local rivals AC Milan on Saturday, keeping them within two points of Serie A leaders Roma.

As their focus turns to a daunting test against the Women's Super League champions, the hosts can draw inspiration from the fact they have won all of their seven competitive home games this season, keeping clean sheets in each of their last four.

While Inter are a point clear of 13th spot, Man City are sitting inside the top 12 on goal difference after starting the main draw with three consecutive draws, making them one of seven teams yet to win in the league phase this season.

The Citizens fought back from two goals down to salvage a 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich before they played out a 1-1 scoreline in their home meeting with Real Madrid.

Man City looked set to claim their first European win of the season when Bunny Shaw netted an 85th-minute penalty against Paris Saint-Germain, only for Tara Elimbi to equalise just three minutes later in a 1-1 draw.

Andree Jeglertz's side have since returned to winning ways with back-to-back Women's Super League victories against London City Lionesses and West Ham United.

Shaw netted a hat-trick in Saturday's comfortable 5-0 victory against the Hammers, sending the Citizens two points clear of Chelsea at the top of the WSL ahead of Saturday's meeting between the two title rivals.

They will be desperate to go into that crucial encounter with their unbeaten away record intact, having won three and drawn two of their five competitive away games this season.

Bugeja will be looking to continue her impressive form after scoring six goals in her previous six appearances for the club, including braces in each of the last two games.

As for Man City, Anna Moorhouse and Alex Greenwood are unavailable for selection after recently sustaining injuries in training.

Vivianne Miedema is closing in on making her return from a knee injury, although Tuesday’s fixture is expected to come too soon for the Netherlands international.
