So there is little sense in buying loads of new players, unless thereai??i??s conclusive evidence that the current crop canai??i??t cut it at the highest level. Seeing how itai??i??s still early days in the reign of Klopp, itai??i??s unlikely he would have been able to reach that conclusion about too many of his players.

In the last two weeks, Klopp has recalled loanees Tiago Ilori (Aston Villa), Sheyi Ojo (Wolverhampton), Ryan Kent (Coventry City), Danny Ward (Aberdeen) and Kevin Stewart (Swindon Town). Against Exeter City, he also utilized all of these players barring Ward, and played youngsters Cameron Brannagan, Joao Carlos Teixeira, Jerome Sinclair, Brad Smith and Connor Randall.

This is exactly what the youth academy is there for, and itai??i??s very pleasing to see Klopp isnai??i??t ignoring it and focusing on the transfer market. That being said, itai??i??s not as if the German should never sign a player. In the transfer market, there are 3 types of signings — the doai??i??s, the donai??i??ts, and the ones you sign only if you absolutely have to.

So then, thereai??i??s only two possible types of players Liverpool should be buying in the winter window:

In the summer windows, one can look at options beyond these two. Your scouting team can have a list of targets, clubs are more open to listening to offers, and you have an opportunity to move out some of your own players to make room for signings. You also have a solid pre-season ahead, so that players who might need to be brought up to speed on the teamai??i??s style of play can be worked with before theyai??i??re thrown into the deep end. January simply isnai??i??t the right time for all this.

So what kind of signings should be avoided? Letai??i??s just call them the a Southampton signingsai??i??. These are the so-called a Premier League readyai??i?? players who seem like an improved version of the current squad, mostly based on their performances in the current season. Some examples of such players would be the likes of Saido Mane, Marko Arnautovic, and Riyad Mahrez. All 3 are talented players, and on paper would make good additions to a side that has not performed well in front of goal. But one good season does not a good player make. Keep in mind that Christian Benteke, Adam Lallana, Dejan Lovren and Roberto Firmino were all their former clubsai??i?? best players, and highly coveted at the time, but none of them have been instant hits at Merseyside. Therefore, to imagine that a January signing will suddenly improve your season is misguided, and you end up paying over the odds as most clubs donai??i??t want to lose their best players mid-way through the season.

One recent transfer rumour has linked Alexandre Pato to a move to Merseyside. What a pointless and risky transfer this would be. Liverpool already have 4 senior strikers on their rolls, excluding Roberto Firmino who can also play up front. Other than Daniel Sturridge, who is one day elder to Pato, all the other 3 are younger than the Brazilian. Before his move to the Brazilian league, his injury record at AC Milan was as bad as Daniel Sturridgeai??i??s. All 4 of the Liverpool forwards have proven themselves either in the Premier League (Ings, Sturridge, Benteke) or the French Ligue 1 (Origi).

Pato is exactly the kind of transfer Liverpool need to steer clear of. Additionally, talks of an early exit from the club for Christian Benteke are ridiculous. The big Belgian has not had time to settle at the club, with his 17 appearances for the club being overseen by two different managers with different styles of playing, and both of these styles being vastly different from how he was played at Aston Villa last season. He deserves till the end of this season at the very least, if not more.

This is the a emergency signinga scenario — a situation all managers (and Boards) hope never arises. For a club with a relatively deep squad like Liverpool, injuries should be the last reason to sign a player, but there are exceptions. For example, the centre-half situation at Liverpool right now. When youai??i??re forced to play Jose Enrique and Tiago Ilori (who started his first competitive game of the season) as the centre-back pairing, the situation is truly dire. One could make a case for signing an experienced centre-half to step in, like Andrea Ranocchia (Inter Milan) and Neven Subotic (Borussia Dortmund), both of whom have been linked with a transfer to Liverpool FC.

Even in such an extreme scenario, seeing how Mamadou Sakho and Kolo Toure may possibly return within the week, these signings make no sense. You donai??i??t spend A?7 to A?10 million on players just to feature in a few games. Hopefully Liverpool FC will make it out of this window without any such expenditures.

History teaches us that short-cuts and quick-fixes can be accompanied by pretty massive pitfalls. Liverpool FC fans need to stop looking to the transfer market for the answers. Jurgen Klopp is at the helm, and his methods require investing time and effort in the players he works with. Heai??i??ll sign players when he comes across the right ones, but hopefully wonai??i??t be spending money searching for some unicorn signing that will miraculously fly the club to success.

And it is absolutely the right approach to take.

#1906. Michael Carrick sack news LIVE: Manchester United latest as shock twist emerges

Manchester United have decided to sack Michael Carrick as manager following the chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford. The under-fire boss was given Sunday’s draw, and the visit of Roma earlier in the week, which saw Man Utd overturn a 2-0 half-time deficit to win in the Champions League, but it hasn’t proven enough to keep his job.

Widespread reports overnight claim that a decision has finally been made, with Carrick set to depart and a new manager be appointed - though a decision may be delayed until Wednesday or Thursday as Sir Jim Ratcliffe has summoned club chiefs to Monaco. There also remain plenty of questions regarding who the new man could be. Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann were considered early frontrunners, and Antonio Conte is said to be keen, but it is Mauricio Pochettino who is now the favourite to land the job.

United head into the November international break sitting inside the bottom three amid genuine fears over a potential relegation battle this season, having won just one of their first 10 matches - at home to newly-promoted Ipswich back in August - and collected only eight points with a tough trip to Liverpool to come next. Whoever come in has an almighty task on their hands. Follow the latest on Michael Carrick’s Manchester United future live below!

Antonio Conte will not become the new Manchester United manager.

That is according to Fabrizio Romano, who reports that the speculation around the former Chelsea and Tottenham head coach moving to Old Trafford has “gone cold”.

The Italian had been heavily linked with a switch to the north west in recent weeks as pressure piled on Michael Carrick after a dismal run of form saw the Red Devils win just once in 11 matches, as they lie in the relegation zone of the Premier League table.

BBC Sport claims that instead of sacking Michael Carrick, Manchester United could turn to strengthening his coaching set-up.

Aaron Danks, the Bayern Munich assistant manager, has been linked with a switch to Old Trafford should that happen, having worked with Carrick at Middlesbrough.

Cole Palmer has previously heaped praise on Mauricio Pochettino, amid a transfer theory involving the Chelsea star.

Pochettino was at Chelsea when Palmer was signed in a deal worth £45million from Manchester City on transfer Deadline Day in September 2023.

To this day, there is a strong argument that Palmer played his best club football under the Argentine.

During their one season together, Palmer was the stand-out player in a youthful Chelsea side, leading the scoring charts with 25 goals in 45 appearances across all competitions.

That form led to Palmer being named Men's Young Player of the Year at the 2024 London Football Awards and it was during the ceremony where he spoke about his relationship with Pochettino.

"He speaks to you about anything, like family issues,” Palmer said. “I think if he knows what's going on off the pitch, it can affect how he is with you on the pitch. He's really great at that.

"He's given me the freedom to play my stuff and I like it when he frees you because I feel I can express my stuff more.

"I'm loving it. Every day he's talking to you about different things, not just football things but life things as well. He's good at making you feel good and trying to get the best out of you."

Mauricio Pochettino is expected to address the media this week, though he is likely to be quizzed about links to Manchester United rather than the USMNT’s upcoming fixture.

Pochettino, who signed a contract extension with the national team back in August - taking him through to the 2030 World Cup, is busy preparing for this weekend’s Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti.

However, the build-up to the game has been somewhat disrupted by talk of the Argentine becoming the next Man United manager.

Following United’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, Pochettino - out of nowhere - emerged as the new leading contender to replace Michael Carrick in the Old Trafford hotseat.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss is now the favourite among bookmakers for the job amid reports Man Utd chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox will recommend a managerial change during a scheduled meeting with the Glazer family and minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

While the possibility of Carrick staying on has not yet been ruled out, a final decision may not come until Thursday - around 24 hours before Pochettino’s pre-Haiti press conference.

Unless more clarity is provided before Pochettino sits down in front of the media to fulfil his usual pre-matchday duties for the USMNT, he will almost certainly be asked about the Man Utd job, thus forcing him to break his silence on the matter.

Manchester United could well be moving towards appointing a new manager.

The Red Devils look set to part company with under-fire head coach Michael Carrick this week, according to widespread reports, with a crisis meeting set to be held in Monaco on Wednesday with club executives including Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox.

Carrick’s position has come under severe scrutiny after just one win in 11 games in all competitions, and United were almost embarrassed at home against Aston Villa at the weekend, falling behind by two goals twice inside the opening minutes of either half.

It was a game that they roared back to draw, with Patrick Dorgu notching an injury-time equaliser, but the level of the overall performance was again cause for concern, with the 20-time Premier League champions mired in the relegation zone after 10 matches.

Michael Carrick is done for the day, with reports he left the training ground an hour ago after overseeing a session with the players not called up for international duty.

Michael Carrick has taken charge of Manchester United first-team training, with the final international break of 2026 officially underway.

Carrick’s presence at Carrington on Tuesday morning came as somewhat of a surprise given widespread reports overnight that he is set to depart as manager.

Instead, an announcement regarding the future of Carrick has been delayed, with BBC Sport reporting that a meeting has been scheduled for Wednesday in Monaco has been scheduled for owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and executives Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox.

Carrick will have been working with a limited number of senior players during training on Tuesday as several members of the Man United first-team squad have been selected for international duty.

Interesting developments regarding Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada.

Despite fierce scrutiny of their positions at Manchester United, Wilcox and Berrada are expected to retain Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s backing .

According to the Telegraph, they still have Ratcliffe’s trust, and a change to their positions is considered unlikely as things stand.

Furthermore, it is understood that Ratcliffe placing his faith in the pair to navigate the club through its current troubles.

This does not bode well for Michael Carrick ahead of Wednesday’s meeting in Monaco as Wilcox and Berrada are expected to recommend a change of manager.

Michael Carrick has already issued a warning to Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada over his "Project 150" plan.

In 2028, Man United will celebrate its 150th anniversary and Berrada has previously gone on record stating the plan to mark the landmark achievement is by winning both the men's and women's league titles.

In an interview with the United We Stand fanzine, he said: "It's establishing a series of targets within a timeframe so we can focus our efforts and energy on that goal.”

Michael Carrick's future as Manchester United head coach is little closer to being resolved.

Despite widespread reports on Monday night claiming a decision has been made to sack the under-pressure manager, Carrick arrived at the club’s Carrington training ground on Tuesday and oversaw training with a depleted group due to international commitments.

It was expected that Carrick would be sacked on Tuesday, with an official announcement to come soon after, but BBC Sport report that it will be at least another day until their is concrete clarity.

Carrick’s future is set to be discussed at a meeting involving Sir Jim Ratcliffe and senior club executives in Monaco on Wednesday.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox on Monday flew out to Monaco for the pre-planned meeting, during which Carrick’s future will be discussed.

BBC Sport add that Berrada and Wilcox are expected to will recommend on Wednesday to minority owner Ratcliffe and the Glazer family that Carrick be dismissed and a new manager be appointed.

A final decision may then not come until Thursday, with Carrick and the club in limbo until official confirmation. Carrick staying has not yet been ruled out.

#1905. Saliba may struggle to dislodge Konsa on Arsenal return, says Ferdinand

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

William Saliba may struggle to get back into Arsenal's starting XI when he returns to full fitness, given the hugely impressive form of recent signing Ezri Konsa.

That is the view of former Manchester United and England centre-back Rio Ferdinand, who believes Konsa's transition since arriving from Aston Villa has been seamless.

Saliba has been sidelined since suffering a back injury during France's defeat to Spain in the World Cup semi-finals, though he played for Arsenal's under-21s last weekend as he nears a return.

But with Konsa joining the Premier League champions and slotting in alongside Gabriel Magalhaes, Mikel Arteta's side have barely noticed Saliba's absence.

Arsenal boast a five-point lead over Brighton at the top of the table, having won nine of their first 10 Premier League matches, and their defensive record has been nothing short of fearsome.

The Gunners have conceded the fewest goals (five), given up the lowest expected goals against figure (7.6 xGA), faced the fewest shots on target (26) and allowed their opponents the lowest xG figure per shot (0.7) and conversation rate (4.5%) among all Premier League sides.

Konsa has appeared in nine of their games, making the joint-most interceptions among their squad (nine, alongside Gabriel and Declan Rice) and winning possession 32 times – only Rice (35 times) has recovered the ball more often.

Konsa will miss England's meeting with Croatia on Thursday but could return from a minor knock in time to face Spain on Sunday, and if the 29-year-old stays fit, Ferdinand feels Arteta will find it difficult to drop him.

Ferdinand said on his YouTube channel: "Mikel Arteta has got a huge problem now. What is he going to do when Saliba is fit?

"Because Konsa has come into that back four and said, 'I have been here for 10 years and I am the immovable object now,' that's what it feels like.

Another top display. Another clean sheet. In Focus: Ezri Konsa edition

"He has just slid in there and said, 'that is my spot, it is mine now'. He has made some last-ditch tackles to keep them in games and to help them win games.

"He looks dominant, aggressive, and he looks accustomed to wearing the Arsenal shirt. He looks like he is meant to be there, but let's not forget about Saliba and what he was doing when he was in the team, how great he looked.

"This is a problem, but it is a problem that Mikel Arteta, I hope, will enjoy – to have two top centre-backs vying to play in that team, who are performing at their best at the moment, and arguably your best one [Saliba] is not in there… what a position to be in."

Arsenal visit Newcastle United for their first game back after the international break, on November 21, before hosting Manchester City in a huge clash between title rivals the following week.

#1904. Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Table-toppers Arsenal travel to Anfield tonight with their first Premier League trophy since the ‘invincibles’ season of 2004 in sight. The Gunners top the table and with stuttering performances from Manchester City and a Leicester City whose fairytale run seems at an end, and are in pole position to finish the current campaign as champions.

While Jurgen Klopp’s men are still finding their way inconsistently since his appointment, Arsenal are in top form with five victories out of their last six matches. In comparison, Liverpool have been as easy to predict as a magic 8 ball, with impressive wins over Leicester City and Manchester City, but accompanied with horrific losses against Watford and West Ham. With fourth place still within grasp and with an impressive record against the table topping teams this season, Liverpool would look to give their long suffering fans some cheer with which to greet this New Year.

The Reds desperately need a victory to steady the ship as their erratic and wayward form sees them enter 2016 still outside the top 4 and distant from any title challenge.

With a host of injuries to his main XI, Jurgen Klopp could be forgiven for dipping into the transfer market so early. The Reds have captured QPR right-back Steven Caulker along with Marko Grujic in the January transfer window.

With Grujic returning to his former club Red Star Belgrade on loan, Steven Caulker is likely to be given a run out as a substitute with the current spate of Liverpool injuries.

Ings, Sturridge, Lovren, Coutinho, Origi and Flanagan are amongst the Liverpool afflicted and will take no part in the match ahead. With Lovren out, Kolo Toure and Mamadou Sakho look likely to be Klopp’s first choice central defending partnership.

Alberto Moreno and Nathaniel Clyne should start as full-backs for the Liverpool side and will be crucial in any attempt to penetrate the Gunner’s defences. Emre Can and Lucas should marshal the midfield, while James Milner, Firmino and Adam Lallana look to give Petr Cech some concerns about his goal. Leading the line should be Christian Benteke, who’s lack of form doesn’t threaten this match as manager Klopp has few options in his position.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Mignolet; Clyne, Sakho, Toure, Moreno; Lucas, Can, Firmino, Lallana, Milner, Benteke.

Arsenal must show that they have the one quality required of all champions : Consistency. The task is hereby straightforward for Wenger’s men. Win, keep winning, regardless of your manner and the title is yours.

With half the season concluded, Arsene Wenger must be wishing that he received a Christmas gift from the Arsenal medical team. Injuries have decimated his midfield with Wilshire, Cazorla, Rosiscky, Coquelin and Sanchez out of the game.

There is some good news with Mesul Ozil having managed to partake in some leisure instead of participating in the FA cup victory over Sunderland. Keeping the nimble playmaker fit would be key to Arsenal aspirations, both in this match and for the remainder of the season.

With both Petr Mertersacker and Gabriel available, it would be interesting to see whom Arsene Wenger picks out for his starting XI. Koscielny, Bellerin and Monreal have nailed down their place in the defence and the inclusion of the slower Mertersacker or the inconsistent Gabriel may have a defining moment in the game.

With Arsenal’s midfield woes, it should fall to Flamini to screen the defence with Ramsey alongside him. Walcott, Ozil and Joel Campbell should be the main thrusts of Arsenal’s attacking play with Giroud as the elegant, decisive focus.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Cech; Bellerin, Gabriel, Koscielny, Monreal; Flamini, Ramsey, Ozil, Walcott, Campbell; Girourd.

With previous encounters between these teams resulting in high scoring draws, we favour a repeat of last year’s epic 2-2 result for the same fixture. Martin Skrtel’s 97th minute header in front of the Kop capped a memorable game which also had Fabio Borini sent off and we expect similar fireworks at Anfield tomorrow.

#1902. Paris Saint-Germain Women vs Bayern Munich Women - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 09 Nov 2026 00:29, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 20:18

Bayern Munich Women will head to the French capital for Tuesday’s Women’s Champions League meeting with Paris Saint-Germain Women at the Parc des Princes.

The hosts start matchday four in sixth spot in the league phase, level on five points with their seventh-placed opponents.

PSG are sitting two points adrift of the top four after winning one and drawing two of their first three league phase games.

The French giants started out with a 1-1 draw against Real Madrid in the Spanish capital before they cruised to a 5-0 home win against Belgian side Leuven on matchday two.

PSG maintained their unbeaten league phase record with a 1-1 away draw against Manchester City, which saw Tara Elimbi net an 88th-minute equaliser not long after Bunny Shaw had opened the scoring from the penalty spot.

Paulo Cesar's charges went on to play out another 1-1 scoreline in their Premiere Ligue meeting with local rivals Paris FC before they returned to winning ways with an emphatic 4-0 victory over Le Havre on Friday, leaving them in second place in the league table.

That commanding win made it five victories without conceding across their last six competitive home games, which should inspire confidence ahead of a difficult test against Bayern.

PSG are looking to record their first European home win against Bayern since running out 4-0 winners in the second leg of a quarter-final tie in March 2017.

Like PSG, Bayern are one of eight teams yet to lose in the 2026-27 league phase after collecting five points from their first three games.

The reigning Frauen-Bundesliga champions kicked off the main draw with a 2-2 draw against Manchester City before they eased to a 3-0 victory over Benfica in Portugal.

Jose Barcala's side then played out a second straight 2-2 home in Europe, fighting back from two goals down to salvage a point against Real Madrid.

They have since returned to winning ways with victories over Bayer Leverkusen and Werder Bremen in the DFB-Pokal Frauen and Frauen-Bundesliga respectively, extending their unbeaten start to the season to 15 games (W13, D2).

In fact, Bayern have not lost a competitive game since falling to a 4-2 defeat against Barcelona in the second leg of their UWCL semi-final tie in May.

They will be hopeful about their chances of extending that unbeaten streak with a win, having prevailed in their last two away games against PSG, including a 3-1 success in last season's league phase.

Thiniba Samoura, Emilie Osteras and Jennifer Echegini are all pushing for recalls after dropping down to the bench on Friday.

#1899. FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

Home » Home 2 » FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

The ban will start from the July transfer window this year and finish with the January transfer market in 2017.

Atletico were also fined 900,000 Swiss francs (820,000 euros) and Real 360,000 (330,000 euros).

“The two clubs were found to have violated several provisions concerning the international transfer and first registration of minor players as well as other relevant provisions with regard to the registration and participation of certain players in competitions,” said a FIFA statement.

Barcelona has just ended a one year ban for similar reasons.

Real and Atletico were “issued with a reprimand and given 90 days in which to regularise the situation of all minor players concerned,” FIFA said. They can still sell players during the transfer ban.

FIFA said the alarm was raised over the two clubs by FIFA’s Transfer Matching System and its disciplinary committee completed the inquiry.

Under international football rules, players under 18 cannot be transferred to another country, except in limited circumstances. All transfers need the approval of a special FIFA committee.

“The investigations concerned minor players who were involved and participated in competitions with the clubs over various periods between 2007 and 2014 (Atletico Madrid) and between 2005 and 2014 (Real Madrid),” FIFA said.

The ban follows a similar sanction handed to European champions Barcelona, who were unable to register new players during 2015.

Barca were initially banned in April 2014, but managed to delay the sanction taking affect until the transfer windows in January and the summer 2015 by launching an ultimately unsuccessful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

By delaying the ban, Barca managed to sign the likes of Luis Suarez and Ivan Rakitic in the summer of 2014 to propel them to a treble of La Liga, Champions League and Copa del Rey.

The news is just the latest institutional embarassment for Real Madrid just over a week after they appointed French legend Zinedine Zidane.

Madrid have sacked two Champions League winning coaches in Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez in the past seven months, as well as being thrown out of the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player.

The sanction could also be bad news for the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United, who had targeted Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale with Real highly unlikely to dispose of their best players without the chance to sign suitable replacements.

La Liga leaders Atletico Madrid’s usually hectic transfer policy will also be put on hold. However, Diego Simeone’s men look better placed to cope with the ban having invested heavily in young talent over the past year.

Neither Real no Atletico made an immediate comment on whether they would appeal.

#1897. Colchester United vs Ipswich Town U21 - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 09 Nov 2026 00:55, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 20:17

Colchester United and Ipswich Town Under-21s will square off on Tuesday in the final round of group-stage games in the EFL Trophy.

Both teams are winless in the competition and unable to advance from the group, leaving them only in search of a confidence-boosting victory.

Colchester United return to action on Tuesday aiming to make it back-to-back cup victories having ended a winless streak at the weekend.

They have endured a tough start to 2026-27, currently sitting 23rd in League Two having earned just 12 points from their first 13 matches while only winning two and losing five of those.

Their last league victory came in late September, and a 12-game winless run also included their first two EFL Trophy outings, losing 3-1 away at Peterborough United and drawing 1-1 against Luton Town before losing the resultant penalty shootout.

That rut then culminated in consecutive league defeats to Northampton Town and Walsall, sending Danny Cowley's side into the relegation zone, before they hosted Worcester City in the FA Cup first round of Saturday and finally bounced back to winning ways as Jaden Williams scored the only goal.

Now unable to advance in the EFL Trophy, but needing to build confidence on the back of that win before turning their focus back to their League Two survival bid, Colchester United will aim to make it consecutive triumphs at the Colchester Community Stadium.

Their visitors, similarly, are unable to go further but will look to record a first win of this season's tournament to go out on a positive note.

Ipswich Town Under-21s began the 2026-27 EFL Trophy with group-stage trips to Luton Town and Peterborough United and struggled to compete on both occasions, firstly losing 6-0 to the latter in September.

John McGreal's side then suffered a 4-1 beating against Peterborough in the second round of games, having fallen 4-0 down before the break before Luca Fletcher netted a second-half consolation.

They have since enjoyed more success in the National League Cup, most recently bouncing back to winning ways with a 5-0 triumph away at Aldershot last week with Frankie Runham hitting a brace alongside goals from Jakubas Mazionis, Josh Lewis and Shakil Nicolaou.

Ipswich Town Under-21s now head to Colchester aiming to put their first two EFL Trophy results behind them and bow out with a first win over league opposition in the competition.

Ipswich Town U21 form (all competitions):

Colchester United fielded a strong starting XI at the weekend for an FA Cup tie against non-league opposition and should line up similarly on Tuesday given their need for a winning run.

Teddy Bishop, Harry Anderson, Kylian Kouassi and Jake Leake will remain sidelined by injuries.

Williams will continue to lead the line after his winning goal against Worcester City, while Jack Payne should continue in support in an experienced midfield unit alongside Jay Williams and Paul Digby.

Ipswich Town Under-21s should field a similar starting XI from their 5-0 win last time out, with regular Luca Fletcher likely to continue up front.

Runham is a danger man on the wing having moved onto six goals for the season with his brace, while Nicolaou has a claim to come in from the start after scoring off the bench.

Mazionis and Charlie Compton are mainstays in defence and midfield respectively.

The young Tractor Boys have their best chance to compete in an EFL Trophy game on Tuesday, and we do see them keeping it close but back Cowley's men to make it-back-to-back wins if he sticks with a full-strength lineup.

Cisse was handed his first Azzurri call-up ahead of their Nations League fixtures versus France and Belgium, following a strong start to his time with the Rossoneri.

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Dejan Kulusevski has revealed that some Tottenham staff doubted that he would be able to recover from the knee injury that kept him out for 18 months.

“I’ll get to play some minutes in both games,” he continued.

“Around 30 minutes in each. That’s what’s been said. It’s better than zero, so I’m happy.”

Home » Home 2 » Sampdoria swept aside by rampant Napoli – are the Partenopei on course for their first Scudetto in 26 years?

Dries Mertens celebrating with his team-mates on the touchline after his decisive goal in the 4-2 victory at Sampdoria is typical of the spirit and togetherness that has seen Napoli storm to the top of the Serie A title. It was in dedication to Chelsea loanee Nathaniel Chabolah who recently lost his mother a a nice touch to show that there is much more to life than football, even though they have put themselves in a wonderful position to end Juventusa dominance and end a 26-year wait for the Scudetto.

Five straight wins have put Maurizio Sarria s team two points clear at the top, with the former Empoli manager breathing a new lease of life throughout a team that have always looked capable of competing for the title, yet ultimately fallen short when the pressure to deliver grew. He has transformed the entire dynamics of how Napoli play, with clinical attacking movement combined with a rock-solid defence within a 4-3-3 system that is getting the very best from the players at his disposal. This seasona s statistics proved that point; Napoli are far and away the highest scorers in Serie A this season, while only Inter Milan and Juventus have a better defensive record. Just one defeat in the twenty league games since the opening day loss at Sassuolo is another illustration of just how good Napoli have been this season, with the crushing 4-0 win at AC Milan in early October a sign of what the Partenopei are truly capable of.

Juventus were always likely to be favourites for the Scudetto on Coral and any other football odds site as their dominance of Italian football threatens to extend into its fifth season, so it is perhaps refreshing from a purista s perspective that Napoli have emerged as real contenders to challenge the Bianconeri. Massimo Allegria s side have stormed up the table in ominous fashion following a surprisingly slow start to the season, with eleven straight victories serving a serious warning to Napoli that they will make them fight all the way for the 2015/2016 Serie A title. It remains to be seen how Sarri and his team handle the pressure of having Juventus breathing down their necks, but the fact they have scored twelve goals in their last three games would indicate that

Some may have been surprised by Gonzalo Higuaina s decision to swap Real Madrid for Naples in the summer of 2013, but the 28-year-old has become one of the most feared strikers in Italy. The Argentine international has formed a wonderful strikeforce at the front of a three-man attack, with Jose Callejon and Lorenzo Insigne adding searing pace and skill on either side of a frontman who has made a career from being a true predator inside the box.

Twenty-one games in as many Serie A games this season puts him amongst the most in-form strikers in world football, with his clinical finish which opened the scoring against Sampdoria proving just how good he has been in front of goal. It is the sort of purple patch that any striker worth their salt would dream to be in; Coral have unsurprisingly backed Higuain as favourite to score in their next game against Sarria s former employers Empoli who have kept just one clean sheet from their last five league fixtures. Napoli will need Higuain to carry his rich vein of form throughout the rest of the season if they are to have any chance of maintaining their wonderful pace and sprint clear of the chasing pack.

Napoli have won many admirers across Europe for the quality of football they have played this season, but it remains to be seen if they have the mentality to pass the acid test and keep the momentum going between now and the end of the season. Recent history would suggest that their chances are not great; the Partenopei, then managed by Walter Mazzarri, put themselves in a wonderful position in 2012/2013, only to finish runners-up behind Juventus as the odd slip at the wrong times proved costly in their pursuit of Juventus. A number of third-placed finishes would also suggest that Napoli have lacked the mentality and guile to end their long wait for a Scudetto, but there is real excitement in Naples that the current crop of players have what it takes to stop the Old Lady from making it five titles in a row.

#1891. Liverpool vs. Man United: Michael Carrick injury boost as "spasm" timeline revealed before Anfield Premier League game

By Lewis Nolan | 09 Nov 2026 01:17

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has confirmed that Harry Maguire should have enough time to recover for their clash with Liverpool after a back spasm.

The Red Devils will enter the international break in 18th place following their 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday, with the club taking just eight points from their first 10 games of the Premier League season.

To make matters worse, centre-back Maguire was replaced at half time at Old Trafford, and fears arose that he could miss the team's match against Liverpool on November 22.

However, Carrick eased those concerns and suggested that the international break could give him enough time to recover, telling MUTV: "Harry had a bad back. A really bad back spasm that he had with maybe 10, 15 minutes to go in the first half.

"I don't know how bad it is but, going into the internationals, there should be plenty of time for him to recover."

Ayden Heaven came on to replace Maguire, though Lisandro Martinez will also be available for United's visit to Anfield.

The game at Anfield could be defining for United for a number of reasons, but none more so than the fact a damaging defeat could be Carrick's last ever match in charge as boss.

There is a chance that he could be dismissed during the international break, though the fixture against Liverpool will still be vital considering a loss would be a worrying way for a new head coach to start their reign.

More concerning is that failure to win could leave the Red Devils last in the table after 11 matchweeks, and that would likely condemn them to a relegation battle for the remainder of the campaign.

A meeting with Liverpool will always be a significant event, but there is far more at stake than just another three points, so having as many players available for that fixture as possible will be important.

Liverpool lead the division in terms of points taken on the road this season (13), but they currently rank 18th for points taken at home (5).

The Reds have already faced Manchester City and Arsenal at Anfield, though it was demoralising for fans to see the team sink to 3-0 and 1-0 defeats in those contests.

A commanding victory against United would be Andoni Iraola's best result of the season, and it would fuel optimism in the fanbase that he could lead the Merseysiders to success.

#1890. EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Home » Home 2 » EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Now that all of the top four English Premier League teams have had a chance to play each other, we find ourselves looking at one of the most wide open title races in recent memory. As of this writing, the league leaders are only separated by a mere six points. With the exception of Manchester City, we could very well see a new face hoisting the Premier League trophy at the end of the season.

For much of the year, it looked like Arsenal would be in the running for its first league title in more than a decade. With the Gunners’ recent victory against Leicester City, they are very much back in the conversation. Danny Welbeck returned to the pitch for the first time this season and made an immediate impact for Arsene Wenger’s squad, scoring the last-minute, game-winning goal to propel the team to within two points of the top spot. Given that even more key players are set to return to action for Arsenal in the coming months, this is easily the best shot they have had of winning a championship since their undefeated 2003-04 season.

Another surprise team that certainly deserves its own mention is Tottenham Hotspur. Following the club’s controversial defeat of Manchester City, the Spurs sit in second place, a mere two points behind Leicester City and ahead of Arsenal on goal differential. Tottenham have yet to win a title in the Premier League era and they have not won an English championship since 1961. The team has done a superb job of backing up star striker Harry Kane with a glut of promising young players, and their goal tally only helps to reinforce the wisdom behind the strategy of manager Mauricio Pochettino.

Meanwhile, Manchester City is still hoping to snag its third title as something of a swan song for exiting manager Manuel Pellegrini. It was recently announced that the club had hired Pep Guardiola . from Bayern Munich to take charge of the team beginning with next season. Thus, Pellegrini has been forced to endure the rest of the campaign as a dead man walking. Despite the impending exit of Pellegrini, City are still in the race for the Premier League title in addition to both the F.A. Cup and Champions League. Theoretically, the club could pull off a treble, if it can manage a solid string of performances during the final half of the season.

At the beginning of the season, it was expected that the usual suspects would once again dominate the league. Many predicted the reigning champs at Chelsea to repeat their success. However, a shocking season has seen the team part ways with controversial manager Jose Mourinho and struggle to remain in the top half of the tables with hopes of a Champions League spot dashed long ago.

For the first time in years, there’s a chance to see a completely new team win the league. No matter which club you support, there’s no denying that this has made for one of the most thrilling contests in recent memory. In a league where money talks, small fish like Leicester City are surprising everyone, and we can only hope that this means a new era of parity for the Premier League.

#1887. Liverpool injury news: Dominik Szoboszlai latest as 'knee' timeline assessed before Man United Premier League game at Anfield

By Lewis Nolan | 09 Nov 2026 02:23, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 02:25

Dominik Szoboszlai has suffered a knee injury and is a doubt for the international break and the games after, Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has revealed.

The midfielder was part of the Reds team that came away from Selhurst Park with three points on Sunday, helping the Merseysiders win 3-1 against Crystal Palace.

However, Szoboszlai appeared to be struggling close to half time with a knee issue, and while he played in the second half, he was substituted in the 69th minute for Trey Nyoni.

Speaking to reporters, Iraola was not sure if Szoboszlai would play any games for Hungary over the international break, saying: "Yes, [Dominik] has, I don't know [if it's] a problem, but he definitely wasn't 100%. Let's see. The last thing we need now is to lose players in the international games.

"Last time, in the international break, we lost three very important players, so now I'm praying. It's the last thing we need. I think he extended a little bit the knee, it was fine, but not 100%, so he has to be careful to see if he can play with the national team or not.

"We will see, and also hope that it doesn't happen like the other break where we lost [Isak], Cody [Gakpo] and Dom. So, touch wood we are in a better place in two weeks."

Szoboszlai has already suffered a hamstring injury, and with Liverpool set to play Manchester United on November 22, Iraola will want the 26-year-old to rest over the next two weeks.

Knee injuries can be complex and involve lengthy periods on the sidelines, but it seems likely that Szoboszlai has avoided the worst possible outcome.

A Grade 1 problem could be a mild sprain, though that would still put the Hungarian's participation in the United game at risk given it would require anywhere from one to three weeks on the treatment table.

It would also make the 26-year-old a doubt for the club's Champions League clash with Club Brugge on November 25, though he would almost certainly be back for the Merseyside derby on November 29.

A Grade 2 injury would involve three to six weeks away from the pitch, and that could leave Szoboszlai unavailable until around Christmas.

Nyoni came on for Szoboszlai against Palace, and the 19-year-old performed excellently, winning two of his three duels and making four defensive contributions, while also playing a significant role in Alexander Isak's goal.

There is an argument that the teenager should be in the starting XI regardless of Szoboszlai's fitness, especially as he has shown he is far more comfortable with the ball in a double pivot.

The youngster was excellent against Arsenal on November 1, and if Nyoni was to play well against United at Anfield, Iraola would find it hard to drop him.

#1885. The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

Home » Home 2 » The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

At the start of this season, John Terry leaving Chelsea was the last thing on anyone’s mind. All was rosy at Stamford Bridge, the home of the newly crowed English champions. In over 21 years at the club, there was no indication that Terry would not retire a Chelsea man.

The Blues’ skipper’s announcement in January 2016, then, came as a shock to the Chelsea faithful, bringing notice to the seemingly premature — even if inevitable — fall of the curtain on a legendary career.

After making his debut in the League Cup against Aston Villa late in 1998, John Terry made sporadic appearances under Gianluca Vialli, before joining Nottingham Forest on a short loan spell. He broke into the first team in 2000-01, when manager Claudio Ranieri handed him 22 Premier League appearances during a season that the 20-year-old would finish as the club’s Player of the Year.

It would be the first of several achievements to come.

Terry’s importance to the team grew as Ranieri relied on his partnership with then-captain Marcel Desailly to mastermind Chelsea’s progression from a fashionable mid-table club to a Champions League team that meant business. They received a major shot in the arm when Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich bought the club in 2003. It was also a significant year in Terry’s international career as he made his England debut against Serbia and Montenegro in June.

The season that followed saw Chelsea finish above perennial winners Manchester United for the first time in Premier League history, and defeat Premiership invincibles Arsenal en route to the club’s first Champions League semifinal. Terry ended the season making a first of four appearances in the PFA Team of the Year, and went to Portugal for the European Championships having displaced Sol Campbell as England’s first choice centre-back.

In the summer of 2004, Chelsea brought in Jose Mourinho, who was fresh from winning a treble with the unfancied FC Porto and raring to take on bigger challenges. The 23-year-old Terry was named captain as Chelsea embarked on the most successful period in the club’s history. In the three seasons that followed, Chelsea won 2 league cups, 2 Premier League titles and the FA Cup — success built on a core of John Terry, Frank Lampard, Petr Cech and Didier Drogba, Chelsea’s ‘old guard’.

This was also a period when Terry picked up several individual accolades. He was named PFA Player of the Year in 2005, the first defender to win the award since Paul McGrath in 1993. He would make a first of five consecutive appearances in the FIFPro World XI in 2005, as well as a first of four appearances in the UEFA Team of the Year.

He was also voted Chelsea’s Player of the Year for the second time in his career in 2006. Steve McClaren, hired as England manager after an underwhelming 2006 World Cup, named the Chelsea skipper as England captain.

Terry was now, beyond argument, one of football’s best.

However, more testing times were to come.

September 2007 saw the departure of Mourinho after a falling out with the club board. The season itself promised much but left a Chelsea squad dejected on three occasions as they saw the League Cup, the Premier League and the Champions League trophies go elsewhere.

For the European Cup in particular, Terry was left with no one but himself to blame as he slipped for the crucial penalty, a moment he has said will haunt him forever. Chelsea and Terry experienced further European heartbreak the following season as Tom Henning Ovrebo had a refereeing performance to forget at Stamford Bridge, handing Barcelona a berth in the final and eventually the trophy.

In early 2010, when he was revealed as the English footballer who had an affair with Vanessa Perroncel, Wayne Bridge’s ex-girlfriend — a horrendous personal error that cost him his status as England captain — it made him the perennial recipient of passionate booing across English grounds. After the revelation, Chelsea travelled to Burnley. Amidst a frosty reception, he scored a late winner to put Carlo Ancelotti’s side back on track in the title race, one they would go on to win in some style. All of this typified John Terry — imperfect, but unshakeable.

Terry had built an unflappable reputation as a top class defender, leader and hard man. He said about himself, “I still say if the ball is there to be won I will go for it, whether with my head or whatever, and if it means us scoring or stopping a goal, I won’t think twice.”

The period that followed, however, was not good for Chelsea or their captain. The team finished the 2010-11 season trophyless, and Carlo Ancelotti paid for it with his job. This was the first of two times in Terry’s career where he and his club would have an extremely underwhelming season following a dominant one, and it also marked the first attempt to phase him out of the first team.

New manager Andre Villas-Boas attempted to introduce a high defensive line that left Terry exposed on a number of occasions, and saw the young Portuguese manager fall back on quicker defenders to implement his system. He was also determined to make lesser use of Frank Lampard and displace Didier Drogba with Fernando Torres. These were unpopular moves that led to poor results and eventually his sacking. Terry was not helped by another personal abberation, mouthing racial profanity at Anton Ferdinand of QPR, an act that saw him land a lengthy ban and damage his position in the England squad almost beyond repair.

Interim manager Roberto Di Matteo reinstated the old guard, and was rewarded with the ultimate prize — the first Champions League in Chelsea’s history.

Terry retired from international football following EURO 2012, leaving him to focus on his club career. However, further rotation was to follow during the reign of Rafael Benitez, who played Terry only in games of lesser importance. This was something he could do with relative impunity owing to the fact that his stock could not have fallen any further among Chelsea fans.

The writing was seemingly on the wall, however. Unsavoury incidents were fresher in the memory than individual accolades, the skipper was out of favour for two seasons running, and was well over 30 years of age. Was John Terry done?

Mourinho did not share the views of Benitez and Villas-Boas. Where they saw a slowing, easily-exposed has-been, he saw an experienced warrior with an excellent reading of the game who could form a title-winning partnership with the quicker Gary Cahill.

Terry grabbed the opportunity he was handed with gusto, performing with excellence in Mourinho’s lower defensive block. The English pair formed the core of a defence that would go on to win the club’s fourth Premier League title in 2015, leading the table from the opening day to the end. It was a landmark achievement for Terry in particular as he played every minute of a league campaign for the first time in his career, aged 34.

Once again they tried to put him down. Once again he fed off it and rose tall.

Chelsea did not start the defence of their title well at all, gathering just 4 points from the first 4 matches. Mourinho, who asked Terry to take the club on his shoulders in 2004 and stood by him for two seasons in his second stint, hauled off his skipper at half-time at the Etihad in the second game of the season, and began to rotate him out of the team, giving an increasing number of starts to the young Kurt Zouma.

The season did not take much of a turn for the better even under interim manager Guus Hiddink, particularly in a defensive sense as the Blues continued to let in goals during a meek climb to the top half of the table, with or without Terry in the side.

A sending off at the Stadium of Light following an injury layoff is not the kind of ending that the fans desired for their beloved captain, who has emerged from the dugout 703 times in Chelsea colours and has been the face of the club through the most successful period in their history.

Offered a new deal by the club last week, the skipper responded, “The contract extension the club has offered me is a different role and I hope everyone will understand I want to take the time to consider it carefully before making a decision.” While fans will hope — for reasons emotional as well as those to do with football — that Terry stays on, the chances look slim.

Should the captain leave the ship, the Blues supporters’ emotions are best summed up by a certain banner that embellishes the Shed End: Captain, Leader, Legend.

#1884. Dowman ban upheld, football’s rules need to change

Let’s start again with Max Dowman whose three match ban was upheld after Arsenal’s appeal against the red card failed. The club had made the bid on the basis of wrongful dismissal and excessive punishment, but the claim was dismissed by an independent regulatory commission who will publish their ‘written reasons’ in due course. Thanks for that.

You will already know I think this is too severe. I thought the sending off was harsh, especially with the video evidence that backed the appeal, and for a player to miss three games for what was such a minor reaction to a heavy challenge is really unfair. And I would say that if this were an Arsenal player or not. It’s another example of how we hear about the concept of player protection all the time, but the reality is there have been countless incidents which could have been used to demonstrate there’s a seriousness about that but it never, ever happens.

How absurd is it that Max Dowman will serve the same ban as Ryan Shawcross got for snapping Aaron Ramsey’s leg in two? Remember when Dan Smith launched himself at Abou Diaby’s ankle, putting him out of the game for 9 months and causing an injury so severe it plagued the rest of the Frenchman’s career? He didn’t even get a red card that day, so the next time you see Dermot Gallagher pontificating on Sky about how a referee got an obviously wrong decision right, apply that context (he was the ref at the Stadium of Light that day).

Football has a problem with actual violent conduct, but chooses to deal with it by trying to make us think performative infractions like Dowman’s are worthy of the same punishment as the acts of real violence. The dangerous tackles, the two-footed leaps (which seem to creeping back into the game a bit, probably because they’re not being punished), pushing an opposition player when they’re in the air, these things are not on the same scale. If what Dowman did is worthy of a three game ban, the next time someone goes studs first over the ball into the shins of their opponent, they should get ten games at least.

But we know that’s not going to happen. Almost as long as this blog has been going (coming up on 25 years now!), I’ve made the case for there to be a sliding scale of punishment for acts that meet the definition of violent conduct. Some things are just more violent than others, but as long as this blanket punishment of three games regardless of the seriousness of the incident is in place, the more those in charge do the game and the players a disservice.

Still, it is what it is now, and Arsenal will have to live without Dowman for the games against Liverpool, Hull City, and the away trip to Newcastle on the far side of the upcoming November Interlull. He could well have been involved at some point this weekend against Liverpool, but now we’re sweating on the fitness of Noni Madueke, with Eberechi Eze the only other option for the left hand side. There are some whispers that Christos Tzolis could be back in contention for Sunday, which would be a very welcome boost, but the forward line looks a bit light for a game of this significance.

Tuesday’s game against Fleetwood will live in the memory because of the giant killing aspect, but for two young Academy players, it’s a night that will hopefully be formative. For Dowman, whether you think what he did was worthy of a red card or not, there’s a lesson to learn about how you react. To be quite honest, I think there’s something to like about the way he was prepared to stick up for himself against a grown man who wanted to ‘leave a bit on him’, as they say. The talented players are the ones who get kicked most though, and it’s something he’s going to have to contend with as his career develops. Just ask Bukayo Saka. The two have plenty of time on their hands right now, and I’m sure it will be part of his footballing education.

The other player is Marli Salmon who probably should have done better on their goal, but for me is less culpable overall than some of the senior players who didn’t perform at the right level. Arsene Wenger once said:

You pay for the education of young players with points. If I play a 20-year old centre back, I know he’ll cost me points during the season and I have to stand up for that. A less talented 28 year old would cost me less points. However, by 23/24 you have a player.

Marli Salmon is 17. He didn’t cost us any points. There’s a long way still go in his development, but I’m sure with the coaching staff they’ll go over what happened against Fleetwood and he will learn from it. It is more difficult for young defenders than young attackers too. A mistake at the top end of the pitch, like Dowman scuffing a shot wide from a position he probably ought to score from, doesn’t feel quite as costly as a forward running off a young defender to score the opening goal of the game. But again, it’s all part of the process, every young player makes mistakes, it’s how you then use them to improve that counts, and I’m sure he’ll do that.

Right, let’s leave it there for now. #1883. Arteta didn’t see the reaction to the reaction but reacts to the reaction to the reaction

Morning all, let’s do a bit of a Saturday round-up ahead of tomorrow’s game against Liverpool which we’ll cover in more detail then.

First, Mikel Arteta responded to the appeal against Max Dowman’s red card, and said:

We’re very disappointed, to be fair, especially with the reckless tackles that he receives – his reaction is minimal in relation to the action. We’re disappointed it hasn’t been overturned having watched it back.

We’ve put every argument on the table to make a case for it – not only the action that is so evident, but when you look back in slow motion, the previous action and Max’s action is clear. Obviously, we have a very different opinion. I think you also have to look at the context of the player, the age and what happened previously.

You already know what I think. Ultimately, there’s only one person who was in any danger of being hurt on that pitch on Tuesday evening, and it was Dowman himself. Arteta said:

It could have been really bad, and we’re lucky today that he hasn’t had a broken foot – that’s clear.

But as we’ve discussed this week, football’s attitudes to things like minor retaliation versus a ‘crunching’ tackle are a bit topsy-turvey, and Dowman is a victim of that. The fact they didn’t even reduce the ban, which there is definitely precedent for, suggests to me they have chosen to overlook what the replays show, and that’s quite disappointing.

Still, it was interesting to hear Arteta reference Dowman’s age when referring to this, then a bit later on suggesting that if he’s going to play with the big boys, he’s not going to get any special treatment because of how young he is. There’s been discussion and debate about the manager giving the 16 year old a bit of an earful on the sideline as he went off, but in this instance he stood behind his ‘tough love’ approach. Referencing the fact Dowman had been sent off for England U19s a few weeks ago for something similar, and the conversation they’d had in the dressing room before they went out, he said:

I haven’t seen the reaction to my reaction, whether it’s positive or negative. But you need to understand the context, the relationship that I have with him and what we discussed just before we went out.

You want to see the reaction of his teammates? When they have to play with 10, you want to see that? This is the environment and this is the reality. Otherwise we are in Disneyland, we are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League at this level and we look after him so much that you cannot imagine. But at the same time we are going to demand of him, like to anybody else, because he needs to earn the right to play. Otherwise the rest of the boys, what are they going to tell me? You need to be fair.

As I said yesterday, hopefully it’s a learning moment for Max, one he can carry forward for when he returns and beyond. Professional football is absolutely ruthless, there will be managers/players who will try and expose that youthful temperament again, and we know how they’ll do it. He’ll get kicked again, they’ll try and bully him again, but next time he’s got to remember that referees are more inclined to punish the guy who retaliates than the one who perpetrates the first offence. It’s upside down, of course, but that’s the environment in which we exist and one he’s got to get to grips with. I suspect that whatever your own view of Arteta’s reaction, that message will have been made loud and clear to Max Dowman this week.

Elsewhere, because this is very, very funny, Aston Villa say they’re going to take legal action against Jamie Carragher for some comments he made on a podcast. Via their official social media channels, they released a statement which said:

Aston Villa will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher for his unacceptable insults about the club and its fans. Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football. Nassef Sawiris, chairman.

Apparently Carragher’s remarks were about Unai Emery potentially joining Man Utd, and pointing out that there is a kind of pecking order in terms of club stature. Which, regardless of the fact United are a mess right now, is unquestionably true in terms of the size of the fanbase, the history etc. Villa are a successful club with good history of their own, but United are – in this general context – a bigger club. Like Barcelona are bigger than Valencia, like Bayern Munich are bigger than Borussia Dortmund, like some side from the Isle of Man third division are bigger than Sp*rs.

How thin skinned and pathetic do the people running Villa have to be to take exception to something Carragher said, to then ruminate on it, decide that legal action is the best course of action, and then make it public? Genuinely it’s hilarious and embarrassing. Also, I’d be quite happy for Emery to take over at United. He’s done a fantastic job at Villa, but as Arsenal fans we know he’s exactly the man you need to take over a club that’s something of a sleeping giant and a mess on and off the pitch. Emery in at Old Trafford all the way, in my opinion. They’d be facing that side from the Isle of Man third division in no time.

Right, I’ll leave it there for this morning. Happy Halloween, I hope your little visitors aren’t too scary later on, and that your dogs don’t freak out with the fireworks too much.

#1882. Chelsea in the race? Nico Paz sets the 2027 transfer market alight, but who can actually afford him?

By Axel Clody | 09 Nov 2026 07:02, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 07:03

Among the best-performing players in Europe since the start of the season, Nico Paz is the dream of many of the continent’s heavyweights. But a three-figure sum in millions (more than £85m / €100m) will undoubtedly be needed to sign the Argentina international.

Nico Paz was the star of the show as Como thrashed RC Lens 9-1 in the Champions League on Wednesday. A key figure for the Italian side for three seasons, the Argentine number 10 lit up the game with his talent, scoring one goal and providing two assists. In his last five outings, the 22-year-old has even accumulated five goals and five assists.

Unsurprisingly, the best clubs on the planet are battling to secure his services and one of them has a competitive advantage: Real Madrid. Real Madrid hold a buy-back clause of £68m (€80m), included when he was sold to Como in 2024 for £56.1m (€66m). It cannot, however, be activated before next summer.

Real Madrid are therefore the favourites to bring back their former player at such a price, while other European giants will probably find it harder to compete.

It is easy to imagine that Como will not sell their star cheaply and will ask for at least £85m (€100m) to let Nico Paz go to another club. That sum seems too high for Barcelona, who have not spent such an amount since 2019, when they signed Antoine Griezmann.

Because of the sanctions that still threaten the club, Manchester City also appear to be out of the running for now. Their rivals Manchester United, meanwhile, have clearly lost some of their lustre and would probably be less attractive in the eyes of the Argentine.

A transfer to Paris Saint-Germain cannot be ruled out, given that the double reigning European champions have the means to pull out such a big sum. Furthermore, the playing philosophy put in place by Luis Enrique would probably appeal to the Argentina star.

The Premier League also remains an avenue to consider. While Liverpool have Florian Wirtz in this role, Chelsea, for their part, are not afraid of stacking up talents (and expensive transfers) and, despite the presence of Cole Palmer, it would not be so surprising to see Chelsea join the race.

For now, Real Madrid appear to be in pole position to sign him in the summer of 2027, but this saga could heat up in the coming months if Nico Paz continues to perform this well.

#1881. Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running

Teenage sensation Max Dowman was the star of Arsenal’s first pre-season match, as he scored one goal and assisted another in a 4-1 victory over Girona.

Dowman, 16, was joined on the scoresheet by new signing Christos Tzolis, who struck with a low effort in his first game since his £34m move from Belgian side Club Brugge.

Established attackers Kai Havertz and Gabriel Jesus also scored for the Premier League champions, who were largely comfortable against opposition from the Spanish second tier.

Here are four things Telegraph Sport learnt from the match:

It was this time last year that Dowman first announced his remarkable talent to the wider world. Then only 15, he sparkled in pre-season and made it clear to Mikel Arteta that he was ready to impact matches at the highest level.

A year on, Dowman is now an established first-team player. He is the youngest ever Premier League winner and the competition’s youngest ever scorer, and he looks set to make even more of a mark this season.

In this friendly against Girona, Dowman created Arsenal’s opening goal with a gorgeous defence-splitting pass for Havertz. He did so after receiving the ball under pressure and spinning into space. Dowman then scored Arsenal’s third with a powerful low drive from the edge of the box.

Dowman is in competition with Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke for a place on the right wing, which means this summer represents a huge opportunity for the teenager. After playing for England at the World Cup, Saka and Madueke will both miss most of pre-season.

Dowman, therefore, has a serious chance of going into the new campaign as the starting right-winger. The Community Shield on August 16 must be a target in his mind.

“We know what he’s capable of doing,” Arteta said. “We want to be more consistent in terms of the performances and the actions that he can deliver, but I think today he had a really good game.”

Arsenal are close to completing a deal for Newcastle United captain Bruno Guimarães but, for now, their only outfield signing of the summer has been Tzolis. This was the Greek winger’s first match in front of supporters and he immediately demonstrated why Arsenal were willing to pay £34m to buy him from Club Brugge.

With Tzolis, it is all about the final product. Goals and assists. He struck 22 times for Club Brugge last season, and registered 29 assists.

How did he produce such impressive numbers? The answer could be seen in his first-half goal against Girona. Receiving the ball on the left wing, Tzolis quickly accelerated towards the penalty area and unleashed a low shot. It was perhaps a more direct approach than Arsenal would usually have seen from Leandro Trossard, the player Tzolis has replaced, and it caught Girona off-guard as the ball deflected into the net.

“I’m very pleased with him,” Arteta said. “First of all, the way he has adapted to the club, to the team. The connection he’s already generating with the boys. I think you’re going to love the player.

“A player who’s very direct. He’s got the goal between the eyes. He has a lot of similarities with Leo [Trossard] in a lot of the things that he can do and the spaces he can occupy. And then the work rate that he has... He’s a boy that comes with so much hunger. He wants to prove himself, it’s a dream for him. And we are here to help him.”

Havertz was one of the few Arsenal players who benefited from playing at the World Cup. His injury issues mean that, unlike most of his team-mates, he did not end the 2025-26 season in a state of exhaustion.

After returning to the pitch in the spring, Havertz enjoyed an impressive end to the campaign for Arsenal. He then performed well at the World Cup, scoring three goals for Germany.

He remains one of Arteta’s favourite players, not least because of his versatility. He started in attack in the crucial end-of-season games in May, but played in midfield against Girona. His low finish, from Dowman’s pass, represented his eighth goal in his last 12 matches for club and country.

Girona’s goal, scored by Arnau Martínez, was perhaps the only alarming moment of this comfortable pre-season victory. Martínez was unmarked from a left-wing corner when he powered a header into Arsenal’s net.

For a group of players who pride themselves on their set-piece prowess, this was a disappointing moment. It also perhaps showed Arsenal’s reliance on their two first-choice centre-backs, William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães, when they are defending crosses into their box.

Gabriel arrived at Arsenal’s pre-season training camp a few days ago, so he should be in good shape by the start of the new campaign. Saliba, though, will be missing for months with a back problem.

Without Saliba’s height and power, will Arsenal be as effective from set-pieces in the opening chunk of the campaign? Coventry City, Arsenal’s opponents on the first night of the season, will undoubtedly look to test the champions in these situations.

The reigning Premier League champions are handed the Costa Brava Trophy, which is half-heartedly lifted into the air by White. There will be far bigger trophies on offer to Arsenal in the upcoming campaign.

Arsenal have cruised to a routine 4-1 win over Girona, with Havertz, Tzolis, Dowman and Gabriel Jesus all finding the net. Arteta will be delighted with his side’s professionalism and ruthlessness.

Meslier takes too long on his goal kick, gifting a corner to Girona. However, the delivery from the hosts is so poor as it flies harmlessly out of play. That sums up Girona’s difficult evening.

There is another round of substitutions for both sides.

Arsenal’s makeshift line-up, which is full of Hale End graduates, is holding firm, with Girona evidently struggling for attacking inspiration. If Arsenal can see out this victory without any injuries, then it would have panned out exactly how Arteta would have wanted.

Girona carelessly give possession away in defence, allowing Nelson to dribble towards the penalty area. The winger floats a cross into the box, which is met by O’Neill, but the forward’s lofted header hits the top of the bar.

With England wingers Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke not returning until later in pre-season, Dowman has a chance to take ownership of the right wing position ahead of the Community Shield. His assist for Kai Havertz, a lovely measured pass after an excellent piece of skill in midfield, was a sign that Dowman means business.

Dowman drifts inside and pops up in the right channel, wriggling past Moreno, before threading a delightful pass through to Havertz. “A lot is happening,” Arteta said. “We all know about the context of this transfer window. From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level.

Sam Dean has the full breakdown of a potential deal for the Real Madrid star and how Arsenal are prepared to continue flexing their muscles in the transfer market in what would be one of the biggest moves in Premier League history.

#1879. Forward line must step up to help deliver first Anfield win in 14 years

After a midweek journey to the north-west for the EFL Cup, we’re back in that neck of the woods today to face Liverpool in the Premier League.

The team news from the press conference was relatively promising, with Declan Rice, Riccardo Calafiori and Christos Tzolis all in training ahead of the game, and Mikel Arteta sounded relatively positive on Noni Madueke who missed out on the trip to Fleetwood Town. With Bukayo Saka out, and Max Dowman obviously suspended, he’ll start on the right and hopefully this run in the team will see him deliver a little more in terms of end product.

He got the backing of the manager beforehand, who said of him reaching his potential:

He has all the potential to do it, he has all the attributes to do it. He certainly has the will to do it because when you see him train every single day, he’s one of the players who enjoys the practice the most and wants to expose himself to all kinds of situations and actions. Now he needs to put the performance on the pitch.

Eberechi Eze should start on the other side, looking for his first Premier League goal contribution of the season, and I think the only other decision to be made is the construction of the midfield. Will it be Myles Lewis-Skelly or Bruno Guimaraes with Rice and Martin Odegaard? My own preference for a tricky away game is probably for Myles, because if you need to change something the Brazilian has attributes you can count on for that. However, he started him away in Munich, brought Lewis-Skelly on in his place when we were 2-1 down and that turned out all right. So, let’s see.

My guess is we’ll see: Raya, Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori, Rice, Guimaraes, Odegaard, Eze, Madueke, Havertz

After two goals in the first three games of the season, Kai Havertz has gone five without a goal in the Premier League, so today would be a good day for him to get back on track and to find some form again. I’d like to see him stay more central, to be something of a focal point rather than drift around the way he likes to. Perhaps when you face good centre-halves as he will today that’s part of how you disrupt them, but right now there’s real focus on our strikers and what they’re delivering (or not delivering as the case might be), and I hope that he, and Viktor Gyokeres when he gets a run later in the game, can produce what we need.

As for today’s opposition they’re still a bit of a work in progress under Andoni Iraola, but they seem to be getting to grips with what he wants. It took him a bit of time at Bournemouth, and the same seems to be true at Anfield, but Liverpool’s only defeat of the season was to Man City, collapsing late on after going down to 10 men. They have a couple of injuries, but in Alexander Isak they have a dangerous centre-forward in good form, and a player who has caused our central defenders plenty of problems in the past. Gabriel and Konsa will have to be at their best today, the sharpness of his movement in the box is really tricky to deal with.

It’s been 14 years since we last won away at Liverpool in the league, something Arteta views as a record to change:

It’s an opportunity. I came here and in many places we were 20, 22 years, 18 years without winning, and we’ve been doing all these things, so on Sunday, that’s the opportunity that we have.

Regardless of how you might feel about going out of the League Cup, you can be sure Mikel Arteta’s pride will have been hurt by both the defeat and the gleeful reaction to it in certain quarters. He will demand a response from his team today, and if that brings about a win at a ground that hasn’t been favourable for us in recent years, then you wouldn’t be at all surprised. Nevertheless, I think today will be a real test for two sides, neither of whom are in tip-top form right now, and two excellent coaches whose connection and friendship goes back years to add an extra dimension to proceedings.

Right, I’ll leave it there for this morning.
